pr.title: research(what-if): preserve verified visual intelligence and production experiments
pr.body:
Preserve 397 historical What If research files (8,221,384 bytes) on a main-based archive-only branch, with two permanent documentation entry points and README navigation. This is archival preservation, not approval of a finished automated production engine. No original MP4/audio/frame media is imported.

## Scope and ancestry

Base: `08e719264e31ecd82de24f8eeb8f065c08359fe5`; head: `badec432bbf5610748123b3f0e0bcb9cdb25fa10`.
Exactly six linear commits and 400 changed paths (399 additions, one README modification). Zero of the 134 inherited Finance-side commits are included. No Finance, Video 003, source-contract, runtime, schema, adapter or observation-index changes. README preserves main's content and adds only two navigation links.

Four archival batches preserve 51 brain files, 258 per-video structured evidence files, 82 production experiment files and six distinct reports/frozen metadata records. Production experiments remain isolated from reference-channel observations; rejected and provisional results remain unchanged. Two new documents (`docs/YIOS_MASTER_PLAN.md`, `docs/AI_SESSION_CONTEXT.md`) describe mission and dated continuation context without superseding underlying evidence. A separate documentation correction pins seven historical Finance/forensics authorities (eight link occurrences) to commit `1adb8129f689207552f0838414e5823e4255bde1`; these are dated authorities, not live Finance state.

## Validation and publication evidence

- All 397 research source/worktree/committed SHA-256 values and byte counts verified; fresh scope/hash recheck before this PR.
- Independent authenticated GitHub retrieval checked all 400 changed file blobs, their SHA-256 values and Git blob identities, six commit parents and branch ref before/after retrieval. This is complete retrieval, not sampling.
- 35 focused local tests passed in 1.00s on this exact candidate: source contract, forensic brain adapter, staging, query and editing/visual intelligence suites. HEAD/content unchanged since that run; no unnecessary rerun.
- JSON/CSV/Python syntax, 50 present release-manifest entries, eight MASTER tables, documentation links and 14-source contract checked.
- Twelve historical CSV-width defects and historical whitespace are intentionally preserved byte-for-byte. Two source identities remain UNRESOLVED. Frozen release PREPARING metadata is historical, not new sign-off.
- Hosted CI: NOT_VERIFIED; no runs at the last verified exact-head check. Local tests do not imply hosted success.
- Binary backup and standalone restoration: NOT_VERIFIED / BLOCKED. Missing frozen release ZIP, 0921.mp4, nine PNGs, narration MP3; external original media, CapCut/fonts/runtime, gray.npy reproducibility, LFS restore, bundle prerequisites and private independent restoration remain unresolved. Git publication is not binary backup.

It does not establish original audiovisual editing or private retention metrics. Follow its [methods](https://github.com/ghilmanITM360/youtube-intelligence-os/blob/1adb8129f689207552f0838414e5823e4255bde1/research/finance-economics-intelligence/METHODS.md) and owner-controlled continuation.

+1. Select a channel and a topic hypothesis from internal evidence; validate factual gaps through separately authorized research. Preserve uncertainty, counterexamples and financial/scientific claim sources.

+## Git, binary evidence and portability
+
+Git stores reviewed code, schemas, documentation, structured research and portable manifests. Original MP4s stay outside Git; large frames, audio, editable binary projects and renders require an owner-approved private storage policy. Historical tracked exceptions are documented in the [repository safety review](audits/WHAT_IF_REPOSITORY_SAFETY_2026-10-09.md); this plan authorizes no removal or history rewrite.

+## Semantic beat map
+
+| Beat | Script anchor | Viewer must grasp |
+|---|---|---|
+| Safety hook | “Before… one safety rule” | Familiar test has safety condition. |
+| Setup/timer | “start the counter…30 seconds” | Timer measures test window. |
+| Repetition/count | “count…stand up…sit down” | One cycle means rise then return to seat. |
+| Unassisted | “unassisted” | Person completes movement alone; no helper shown. |
+| Unsafe/dizziness/ataxia | “unsafe…dizziness or ataxia” | Any named warning means stop, shown as generic unsteadiness only. |
+| Stop | “don't do this test” | Test ends, no extra rep. |
+| Result | “Once you have your number” | Personal count belongs to one person. |
+| Universal comparison | “don't compare…universal number” | One person's score is not one shared cutoff for everyone. |
+| Low concern | “score looks low” | Viewer may worry about result. |
+| Non-diagnosis | “number alone doesn't diagnose you” | Score cannot directly become diagnosis. |

+"""Build the measured chair-test edit as native CapCut timeline materials.
+
+Uses a CapCut-created image/audio/text sample from Timeline 02 as schema source.
+Writes a replacement draft JSON to the workspace for review before installation.
+"""
+
+from __future__ import annotations
+
+import copy
+import json
+import math
+import uuid
+from pathlib import Path
+
+ROOT = Path('/Users/ghilmankhan/Movies/CapCut/User Data/Projects/com.lveditor.draft/0921')
+TIMELINE = Path(__file__).with_name('timeline_02_before_edit.json')
+OUT = Path(__file__).with_name('chair_test_completed_draft.json')
+DOWNLOADS = Path('/Users/ghilmankhan/Downloads')
+FPS = 30
+END = 34.4
+INK = '#252321'
+RED = '#B94E4A'
+
+def uid(): return str(uuid.uuid4()).upper()
+def frame(t): return round(t * FPS)
+def micro(t): return round(frame(t) * 1_000_000 / FPS)
+
+draft = json.loads(TIMELINE.read_text())
+video_sample = next(t for t in draft['tracks'] if t['type'] == 'video')
+text_sample = next(t for t in draft['tracks'] if t['type'] == 'text')
+audio_track = next(t for t in draft['tracks'] if t['type'] == 'audio')
+video_segment = video_sample['segments'][0]
+text_segment = text_sample['segments'][0]
+video_material = draft['materials']['videos'][0]
+text_material = draft['materials']['texts'][0]
+
+draft['tracks'] = []
+draft['materials']['videos'] = []
+draft['materials']['texts'] = []
+draft['canvas_config'] = {'ratio': '9:16', 'width': 1080, 'height': 1920, 'background': None}
+draft['fps'] = {'num': 30, 'den': 1}
+draft['duration'] = micro(END)
+
+asset_ids = {}
+def asset(filename):
+    if filename not in asset_ids:
+        mat = copy.deepcopy(video_material)
+        mat['id'] = uid()
+        mat['path'] = str(DOWNLOADS / filename)
+        mat['material_name'] = filename
+        mat['width'] = 941
+        mat['height'] = 1672
+        mat['local_material_id'] = uid()
+        asset_ids[filename] = mat['id']
+        draft['materials']['videos'].append(mat)
+    return asset_ids[filename]
+
+def track(kind):
+    sample = video_sample if kind == 'video' else text_sample
+    t = {k:copy.deepcopy(v) for k,v in sample.items() if k != 'segments'}
+    t['id'] = uid()
+    t['segments'] = []
+    t['type'] = kind
+    draft['tracks'].append(t)
+    return t
+
+background = track('video')
+visual_tracks = []
+label_tracks = []
+caption_track = track('text')
+
+def available(tracks, kind, a, b):
+    for t in tracks:
+        if all(s['target_timerange']['start'] + s['target_timerange']['duration'] <= micro(a)
+               or s['target_timerange']['start'] >= micro(b) for s in t['segments']):
+            return t
+    t = track(kind)
+    tracks.append(t)
+    return t
+
+def add_image(filename, a, b, scale=1, x=0, y=0, base=False):
+    s = copy.deepcopy(video_segment)
+    s['id'] = uid()
+    s['material_id'] = asset(filename)
+    s['target_timerange'] = {'start':micro(a), 'duration':micro(b)-micro(a)}
+    s['source_timerange'] = {'start':0, 'duration':micro(b)-micro(a)}
+    s['clip']['scale'] = {'x':scale, 'y':scale}
+    s['uniform_scale'] = {'on':True, 'value':scale}
+    s['clip']['transform'] = {'x':x, 'y':y}
+    s['render_index'] = 0
+    t = background if base else available(visual_tracks, 'video', a, b)
+    t['segments'].append(s)
+    return s
+
+def add_text(value, a, b, x=0, y=0, size=28, color=INK, caption=False, scale=1):
+    # CapCut's native font-size unit renders much larger than a canvas pixel.
+    size = max(8, round(size * .36))
+    m = copy.deepcopy(text_material)
+    m['id'] = uid()
+    m['type'] = 'text'
+    m['name'] = value
+    m['text_color'] = color
+    m['font_size'] = float(size)
+    m['text_size'] = size
+    m['has_shadow'] = False
+    m['shadow_alpha'] = 0.0
+    m['use_effect_default_color'] = False
+    m['alignment'] = 1
+    m['font_path'] = '/Applications/CapCut.app/Contents/Resources/Font/SystemFont/en.ttf'
+    m['font_name'] = 'System'
+    m['fonts'] = []
+    m['content'] = json.dumps({'styles':[{'fill':{'alpha':1.0,'content':{'render_type':'solid','solid':{'alpha':1.0,'color':[int(color[i:i+2],16)/255 for i in (1,3,5)]}}},'font':{'id':'','path':m['font_path']},'range':[0,len(value)],'size':float(size)}], 'text':value},separators=(',',':'))
+    m['base_content'] = m['content']
+    draft['materials']['texts'].append(m)
+    s = copy.deepcopy(text_segment)
+    s['id'] = uid()
+    s['material_id'] = m['id']
+    s['target_timerange'] = {'start':micro(a), 'duration':micro(b)-micro(a)}
+    s['clip']['transform'] = {'x':x, 'y':y}
+    s['clip']['scale'] = {'x':scale, 'y':scale}
+    s['uniform_scale'] = {'on':True,'value':scale}
+    s['caption_info'] = None
+    (caption_track if caption else available(label_tracks,'text',a,b))['segments'].append(s)
+    return s
+
+# Background resets at semantic boundaries. No transitions or source-video layer.
+cuts = [0,6.13,14.87,19.06,20.76,24.46,29.12,END]
+for a,b in zip(cuts,cuts[1:]): add_image('BG_01_offwhite.png',a,b,base=True)
+
+# SH01: simple test; safety condition interrupts.
+add_image('CHAIR_01.png',1.52,6.13,.72,-.24,-.10)
+add_image('STOPWATCH_OUTLINE_01.png',.88,6.13,.48,.30,.29)
+add_text('30 s',.88,6.13,.34,.29,34)
+hook_warning = add_image('WARNING_TRIANGLE_01.png',3.70,6.13,.38,.55,0)
+hook_warning['common_keyframes'].append({
+    'id':uid(), 'material_id':'', 'property_type':'KFTypeScaleX',
+    'keyframe_list':[
+        {'id':uid(),'curveType':'Line','time_offset':0,
+         'left_control':{'x':0.0,'y':0.0},'right_control':{'x':0.0,'y':0.0},
+         'values':[.342],'string_value':'','graphID':''},
+        {'id':uid(),'curveType':'Line','time_offset':micro(4/FPS),
+         'left_control':{'x':0.0,'y':0.0},'right_control':{'x':0.0,'y':0.0},
+         'values':[.38],'string_value':'','graphID':''}]
+})
+
+# SH02: chair never moves. Hard anatomy replacements.
+add_image('CHAIR_01.png',6.13,14.87)
+add_image('PERSON_SEATED_01.png',6.13,11.36)
+add_image('PERSON_STANDING_01.png',11.36,13.58)
+add_image('PERSON_SEATED_01.png',13.58,14.87)
+add_image('STOPWATCH_OUTLINE_01.png',7.30,14.87,.38,.37,.39)
+add_text('30 s',8.30,14.87,.40,.39,30)
+add_text('1',11.64,13.58,-.41,.30,33)
+add_text('2',13.80,14.87,-.41,.30,33)
+
+# SH03: steady, static person. Warning state arrives on spoken cues.
+add_image('CHAIR_01.png',14.87,19.06)
+add_image('PERSON_SEATED_01.png',14.87,19.06)
+add_image('UNSTEADY_ARCS_01.png',16.20,19.06,1,-.34,0)
+add_image('WARNING_TRIANGLE_01.png',17.36,19.06,.30,.55,.45)
+
+# SH04: discrete stop punctuation.
+add_image('STOPWATCH_OUTLINE_01.png',19.06,20.76,.55,0,.20)
+add_image('WARNING_TRIANGLE_01.png',19.06,20.76,.25,.37,.34)
+add_text('DO NOT TEST',19.20,20.76,0,-.25,40,RED)
+add_text('×',19.20,20.76,0,.20,72,RED)
+
+# SH05: one personal score and multiple people. Reject common cutoff logic.
+add_image('SCORE_CARD_EMPTY_01.png',20.76,24.46,.65,0,.41)
+add_text('YOUR SCORE',21.30,24.46,0,.49,25)
+for x in [-.38,0,.38]:
+    add_image('PERSON_STANDING_01.png',22.28,24.46,.27,x,-.12)
+add_text('ONE NUMBER FOR EVERYONE',22.76,24.46,0,-.47,24)
+add_text('≠',23.16,24.46,0,.12,48,RED)
+
+# SH06: connection drawn, then rejected. No numerical threshold.
+add_image('SCORE_CARD_EMPTY_01.png',24.46,29.12,.75,0,.36)
+add_image('DIAGNOSIS_CARD_EMPTY_01.png',25.98,29.12,.85,0,-.15)
+add_text('YOUR SCORE',24.46,29.12,0,.45,25)
+add_text('DIAGNOSIS',25.98,29.12,0,-.23,20)
+add_text('↓',26.74,27.56,0,.11,48)
+add_text('≠',27.56,29.12,0,.11,56,RED)
+
+# SH07: illustrated text conclusion. No invented portrait or branding.
+add_image('SCORE_CARD_EMPTY_01.png',29.12,END,.55,0,.29)
+add_text('YOUR SCORE',29.12,END,0,.35,28)
+add_text('Interpret the score properly',30.76,END,0,-.02,28)
+add_text('Full video on channel',31.96,END,0,-.29,32)
+
+# Verbatim speech in readable thought groups. Caption-safe lower band.
+captions = [
+ (0,.88,'Before you try the'),(.88,2.56,'30-second chair stand test,'),
+ (3.04,4.40,'there is one safety rule'),(4.40,5.38,"you shouldn't ignore."),
+ (6.14,8.06,'So, start the counter,'),(8.06,9.10,'up to 30 seconds.'),
+ (9.54,10.58,'Try to count the number'),
+ (10.58,11.36,'of times that you can'),
+ (11.36,12.40,'stand up on the chair'),
+ (12.40,13.04,'unassisted'),
+ (13.04,14.14,'and then sit down.'),
+ (14.88,16.68,'However, if you feel unsafe,'),
+ (16.68,17.36,'if you got'),
+ (17.36,18.62,'dizziness or ataxia,'),(19.06,20.26,"then don't do this test."),
+ (20.76,22.28,'Once you have your number,'),
+ (22.28,23.16,"don't compare that to"),
+ (23.16,24.02,'universal number.'),
+ (24.46,26.28,'And even if your score looks low,'),
+ (26.74,27.56,'that number alone'),
+ (27.56,28.64,"doesn't diagnose you."),
+ (29.12,30.76,'Dr. Rehan explains how to'),
+ (30.76,31.68,'interpret it properly'),
+ (31.68,33.04,'in the full video on the channel.')]
+for a,b,value in captions:
+    add_text(value,a,b,0,-.77,22,INK,caption=True)
+
+for t in draft['tracks']:
+    t['segments'].sort(key=lambda s:s['target_timerange']['start'])
+draft['tracks'].append(audio_track)
+
+ids = {m['id'] for group in draft['materials'].values() if isinstance(group,list) for m in group if isinstance(m,dict) and 'id' in m}
+for t in draft['tracks']:
+    for s in t['segments']:
+        assert s['material_id'] in ids
+        assert s['target_timerange']['duration'] > 0
+assert len(background['segments']) == 7
+OUT.write_text(json.dumps(draft,ensure_ascii=False,separators=(',',':')))
+print(OUT)
+print('tracks',[(t['type'],len(t['segments'])) for t in draft['tracks']])
+print('materials',len(draft['materials']['videos']),len(draft['materials']['texts']),len(draft['materials']['audios']))

+
+## Visual argument
+
+A familiar physical action is interrupted by a safety condition. One clearly demonstrated action produces one illustrative tally. The tally becomes a personal record. An oversized rubber stamp tries to turn that record into a universal judgment, then into a diagnosis; both shortcuts fail. The record unfolds into a larger explanation shared with another person. +## Authority and scope

+**Actual source MP4 frames outrank forensic descriptions, reconstruction prompts, aggregate DNA, and the rejected prototype.** The coffee/heart test is not evidence here. This fingerprint is based on 112 newly extracted overview frames from all 14 source files, 59 curated frames, targeted multi-state sequences in every source, and 42 existing forensic frame/contact-sheet selections. +
+Source titles, paths, timestamps and images are in [REFERENCE_FRAME_STUDY.md](REFERENCE_FRAME_STUDY.md). IDs R02–R15 identify the 14 sources; R01 is unused. +Every conclusion uses one of these categories:
+
+- **MEASURED / OBSERVED ACROSS CORPUS:** coverage of all 14 source files or an explicitly defined aggregate dataset. A sampled observation is not an every-frame claim.
+- **OBSERVED IN MULTIPLE EXAMPLES:** named supporting images, with no assertion that every source follows it.

+## Human figures
+
+**OBSERVED IN MULTIPLE EXAMPLES — fundamental construction.** R02 at 2.016, 56.443 and 96.760 s; R09 at 0.949 and 6.644 s; R13 at 1.762 and 36.995 s; R04 at 2.183 and 15.283 s show an unfilled circular or slightly oval head, a single narrow torso stroke, single-stroke arms and legs, and elbows/knees made by bends rather than outlined anatomy. Most selected heads have no eyes, nose or mouth. Hands often terminate as a short stroke. Feet can be a bent terminal line; detailed shoes are unnecessary. The figure can be expressive without facial features.
+
+**OBSERVED IN MULTIPLE EXAMPLES — poses explain relations.** A head tilted toward a hand conveys frustration at the keyboard (R02 56.443); extended arms register a reaction to the changed display (R04 15.283); hands at the head register alarm while the diagram itself changes (R13 31–37); a mug is discarded after an imagined consequence (R09 3–7). +**NEW CREATIVE DECISION.** V2 uses registered pose replacements, short physical translations of stamp/paper and a two-state unfolding drawing. No image-to-video generation is required. No continuous sway, generic entrance presets, elastic bounces or routine zooms. Brief state changes must alter meaning, not merely increase motion density.
+
+## Humor and payoff
+
+**OBSERVED IN MULTIPLE EXAMPLES.** An impossible thought changes a mundane action (R09 mug); a small physical effect is compared to a squirrel movement (R02); an escalating diagram intrudes on its own presenter (R13); sunset extension becomes a human-scale joke (R06); a scientific explanation concludes with an unexpected local scene (R15). Humor is in the inference or consequence, not in dressing a generic character brightly.
+
+**NEW CREATIVE DECISION.** V2's oversized stamp embodies the temptation to apply a result indiscriminately and label someone immediately. It is prevented from touching the paper. The final unfolded sheet shows why an isolated count needs explanation. These metaphors have not been found verbatim in the references; they borrow transformation, reaction, object continuity and changing scale. Safety beats themselves stay restrained.
+
+## Conflicts caught in old documentation
+
+1. R02 at 70.554 s visibly shows the headset gamer; the master time lookup returns F10.1's calendar composition. At 56.443 s the visible book pile is missing from part of the legacy description. Raw timestamps are used instead of pretending these rows match.
+2. R03 at 29.190 s visibly shows a standing explorer/shovel scene, while the lookup describes a triptych. At 116.760 s the visible phone gag does not agree with a literal reading of the associated narration sentence as a picture description.
+3. R07 at 42.531/127.593/212.654/255.185 s visibly shows reactor/turbines/source comparison/reactor-vial imagery; several corresponding master rows point to different later scenes, including credits. Those state IDs are not adopted as proof.
+4. R10 at 220.938 and 265.125 s visibly shows the 1G/6G body comparison and board diagram respectively, not the retrieved toxicity chart/space description.
+5. R13's image prompt specifies dot eyes and mouth. The inspected presenter frames show blank heads. The pixels win.
+6. A zero gap between timeline clips does not establish absence of an opacity fade inside those clips. Source-specific rebuild files describe local fades, and sampled R07 states visibly dissolve. Do not repeat the global “zero fades exist” claim.
+7. The old typing manifest says no audio, while the actual repository MP4 probes with audio and later semantic transcripts exist. Historical manifests are not current media truth.
+
+These conflicts do not prevent a visual study. They do prevent using legacy IDs as unquestioned evidence. Every selected frame is addressable by actual source filename plus extraction timestamp; uncertain legacy mappings are marked separately.
+
+## V2 acceptance criteria
+
+- At thumbnail size, participant reads as a blank-headed line figure, not recolored corporate anatomy.
+- Seated/leaning/standing/paused/stopped scenes share chair, ground line, proportions and drawing treatment.
+- Every reveal adds a fact, demonstrates a consequence or denies a false inference.
+- The count remains one person's count; no threshold, diagnosis, age rule or sex rule is invented.
+- Warning ends action. No collapse, symptom loop or continued unsafe repetition.
+- Two comparison figures are large, distinct actors handling records, not duplicated pictograms.
+- Final image resolves the number-only problem visually; it does not dissolve into a text slide.
+- Approval depends on generated images alongside the cited frames. Prompt compliance alone is not proof of visual fidelity.

+# Animation Prompts
+
+One short prompt per motion. Each describes only what changes over time. None
+repeats the frame description — that lives in `VISUAL_STATES.csv`.
+
+All 17 are executed in CapCut. None is an image-to-video generation, so these
+are editor instructions, not I2V prompts. See `I2V_DECISIONS.md`.
+
+**Camera: locked for the entire video. No pan, no zoom, no push-in, no drift,
+no parallax, in any of the 17 motions.**
+
+---
+
+### A01 — Fork and first label appear
+The fork lines, the left label plate and the GOOD? text become visible together in a single frame.
+Everything else — coffee mug, heart, background, camera — stays completely static.
+
+### A02 — Second label appears
+The right label plate and the BAD? text become visible together in a single frame.
+The mug, heart, fork lines, left plate and its text stay completely static. No camera movement.
+
+### A03 — Dr. Rehan appears
+The doctor figure becomes visible in the lower-left field in a single frame, already in final position — no walk-in, no slide, no scale-up.
+The entire binary diagram above him stays completely static. No camera movement.
+
+### A04 — Strike stroke draws across the fork
+The red stroke draws itself on progressively from its lower-left end to its upper-right end, revealed by a wipe along its own path, over roughly 0.5 seconds.
+The mug, heart, fork, both plates, both text labels and Dr. Rehan stay completely static. No camera movement.
+
+### A05 — Energy-drink can appears
+The can becomes visible standing on the right of the baseline in a single frame, already in final position and scale.
+The mug, its two strokes and the baseline stay completely static. No camera movement.
+
+### A06 — Can's stimulation strokes appear
+All four strokes above the can become visible together in a single frame — they do not appear one by one and they do not grow.
+The can, the mug and the mug's two strokes stay completely static. No camera movement.
+
+### A07 — Caution mark appears
+The red caution triangle becomes visible above the can in a single frame. It does not pulse, flash, shake or scale.
+The can, mug and both stroke groups stay completely static. No camera movement.
+
+### A08 — Patient appears
+The patient figure becomes visible in the right field in a single frame, already in final position — no entrance movement.
+Dr. Rehan and the binary diagram stay completely static. No camera movement.
+
+### A09 — Strike stroke draws across the consultation diagram
+The red stroke draws itself on progressively from its lower-left end to its upper-right end, revealed by a wipe along its own path, over roughly 1.0 second.
+Both figures, the diagram, the plates and their text stay completely static. No camera movement.
+
+### A10 — The binary model is deleted
+The mug, both branch lines, both plates, both text labels and the red stroke all disappear together in a single frame, leaving empty off-white. No fade, no shrink, no slide-off.
+Dr. Rehan and the patient stay completely static. No camera movement.
+
+### A11 — Left arrow draws
+The arrow draws itself on progressively along its curve, from the mug down and to the left, arriving at the left figure's chest, over roughly 0.4 seconds.
+The mug, both figures and the baseline stay completely static. No camera movement.
+
+### A12 — First response arc appears
+The single red arc becomes visible at the left figure's chest in a single frame. It does not pulse or repeat.
+The mug, both figures and the left arrow stay completely static. No camera movement.
+
+### A13 — Right arrow draws, then three arcs appear
+The right arrow draws itself on progressively along its curve from the mug down and to the right over roughly 0.4 seconds; the moment it lands, all three red arcs become visible together at the right figure's chest in a single frame.
+The mug, both figures, the left arrow and the left figure's single arc stay completely static. No camera movement.
+
+### A14 — First factor fills
+The gauge icon and the BLOOD PRESSURE text become visible together inside the top plate in a single frame.
+All three plates, the connector line and Dr. Rehan stay completely static. No camera movement.
+
+### A15 — Second factor fills
+The heart icon and the HEART RESPONSE text become visible together inside the middle plate in a single frame.
+All three plates, the connector line, the top plate's contents and Dr. Rehan stay completely static. No camera movement.
+
+### A16 — Third factor fills
+The three-cup icon and the QUANTITY text become visible together inside the bottom plate in a single frame.
+All three plates, the connector line, the top and middle plate contents and Dr. Rehan stay completely static. No camera movement.
+
+### A17 — Factor list swaps to video card
+The three plates, all their icons and text, and the connector line all disappear in the same single frame that the video card, its play mark and the WATCH THE FULL VIDEO text become visible. One instantaneous swap, no fade, no crossfade, no slide.
+Dr. Rehan and the background stay completely static. No camera movement.

+# CapCut Build Plan
+
+Project: 2160 × 3840 (9:16). One audio layer, the unmodified narration. Camera
+locked for the whole video — no keyframed scale or position on any base plate.
+
+**Global rules (from the frozen brain):**
+- Every shot boundary is a **hard cut**. No transition effect of any kind is
+  applied anywhere. (`DECISION_RULES.md` §7 — all 186 corpus shot boundaries
+  measure a 0.0s gap; zero fades exist.)
+- Every reveal is an **opacity on/off at a single frame** or a **wipe mask
+  along a fixed path**. No fade-in, no scale-in, no slide-in, no rotation.
+  (`CAPCUT_PRODUCTION_SYSTEM.md` §1.)
+- All words are **native text layers**. Nothing is baked into a generated
+  image. (`ASSET_CREATION_SYSTEM.md`: 18/31 TEXT_SYSTEM rows are native editor
+  text layers.)
+- Reveals are placed on the **onset of their anchor word**, read off the
+  waveform once narration is recorded. (`AUDIO_VISUAL_SYNC_DNA.md`:
+  STATE_CHANGE median offset 37ms, 95.7% within 300ms.)
+- Narration is never cut, shortened or gap-trimmed.
+  (`CAPCUT_PRODUCTION_SYSTEM.md` §4.)
+
+---
+

+4. G02b — right label plate (transparent PNG)
+5. T02 — text layer `BAD?`

+# Final Visual Production Plan — Coffee / Heart Short
+
+**Everything needed to build this Short is in this one document.**
+
+| | |
+|---|---|
+| Format | 9:16 vertical, 2160 × 3840 |
+| Script | unchanged, verbatim, 130 words |
+| Estimated runtime | 33.1s ESTIMATED (130 ÷ 3.93 words/sec, the measured rate of the frozen corpus's 8 portrait videos). No measured timings exist — nothing here is a real timestamp. |
+| Shots | 5 |
+| Base images to generate | 5 |
+| Visual states | 22 |
+| Motions | 17, all CapCut |
+| Image-to-video generations | 0 |
+| Transitions | 5 hard cuts, no fades anywhere |
+| Camera | locked for the entire video |
+| Visual grammar source | frozen Production Intelligence Brain v1.0.0 only |
+
+---
+
+## Before you start: the visual language, once
+
+Written out here so no prompt below has to say "xkcd style".
+
+**Canvas.** Flat off-white full-frame field. No texture, gradient, vignette,
+border or panel. One visual idea per frame, large forms, generous empty space.
+
+**Line.** Simple thin black hand-drawn linework, slightly imperfect and
+naturally uneven, uniform weight throughout, flat 2D, no perspective, no
+shading, no lighting, no drop shadows.
+
+**Figures.** Minimal stick figures. Plain round circle heads. No faces at all,
+except Dr. Rehan, who is identified by exactly three cues: two small
+rectangular spectacle lenses joined by a bridge, a short solid beard arc under
+the chin, and one short side-swept hair stroke on top. He reads as "a doctor",
+not as a likeness of anyone.
+
+**Colour, strictly rationed.**
+- **Coffee brown** — only ever the liquid band inside a cup.
+- **Muted medical red** — only on the two strike strokes, the one caution
+  triangle, and the response arcs. Nothing else is red, ever.
+- **Light neutral grey** — available but not used in this plan; nothing needed it.
+- No red is generated into any base image. All red arrives as an editor overlay.
+
+**Motion.** Elements pop on in a single frame, or a stroke draws itself along
+its own path. Nothing fades, scales, slides, rotates, pulses or glows. The
+camera never moves.
+
+**Text.** No image prompt asks for a single letter. Every word in the finished
+video is a CapCut native text layer.
+
+*Brain basis: `VISUAL_DNA.md` (89.8% LOCKED/STATIC camera), `MOTION_DNA.md`
+(instant/<0.5s is the largest motion bucket), `DECISION_RULES.md` §7 (zero
+fades across 186 corpus shot boundaries), `ASSET_CREATION_SYSTEM.md`
+(CHARACTER 96% transparent PNG; TEXT_SYSTEM = native editor text layers).*
+
+**Medical guardrails applied throughout (web-verified, not brain-derived).**
+No blood-pressure numbers, no caffeine milligrams, no dose thresholds, no
+diagnoses, no ECG or arrhythmia traces, no disease labels, no skull, death
+icon, flatline, exploding heart or emergency-red frame. The energy-drink
+section gets exactly one outline caution triangle over one object, because the
+narration says "a bit more dangerous", not "dangerous". Coffee is never shown
+as universally good or universally bad. Independently consistent with
+[AHA: Caffeine and Heart Disease](https://www.heart.org/en/healthy-living/healthy-eating/eat-smart/nutrition-basics/caffeine-and-heart-disease)
+and [AHA: energy drinks and blood pressure](https://www.heart.org/en/news/2019/05/29/energy-drinks-may-provide-jolt-to-heart-function-blood-pressure),
+which describe higher-caffeine products as raising risk of high blood pressure
+or irregular rhythm, and describe caffeine response as varying by genetics,
+metabolism, age and prior use — i.e. the script's own central claim.
+
+---
+
+# VISUAL 01 — The binary question

+# Image-to-Video Decisions
+
+Every candidate movement in this Short was evaluated individually. Result:
+
+```
+I2V_REQUIRED = 0
+CAPCUT_MOTIONS = 17
+I2V_MOTIONS = 0
+STATIC (cut-entry states with no motion) = 5
+```
+
+Per the test protocol §31 this is an acceptable outcome, and it is the outcome
+the frozen brain actually points to. It was not forced in either direction.
+
+## The rule applied
+
+`IMAGE_TO_VIDEO_SYSTEM.md` §2 is explicit about which motions have a case for
+I2V: only `SEQUENTIAL`, `SIMULTANEOUS_COUPLED`, `SIMULTANEOUS_INDEPENDENT` and
+`PERSISTENT_LOOP` motions (203/438, 46% of the corpus) describe a genuine
+multi-frame organic progression. `STATE_REPLACEMENT` (230/438, 53%) is by
+definition one static illustration discretely swapped for another and
+"should remain deterministic image swaps, not I2V-generated."
+
+`DECISION_RULES.md` §7 adds the hard constraint: every one of the corpus's
+186 shot boundaries measures a 0.0s gap, and no fade, dissolve or wipe exists
+anywhere. I2V generation cannot guarantee an exact frame-accurate end state
+or an untouched static anchor — it interpolates. In a video whose entire
+grammar is "exact geometry held in a locked frame, changed on a word," that
+interpolation is a defect, not a feature.
+
+## Per-motion decision
+
+| Motion | Movement | USE_I2V | Why |
+|---|---|---|---|
+| A01 | Fork + plate + text appear | NO | Discrete visibility change. Exact line geometry and exact text position required. |
+| A02 | Second plate + text appear | NO | Same. Must be pixel-identical in size and stroke to A01's plate — generation would not hold that. |
+| A03 | Dr. Rehan appears | NO | Character entry is a one-frame opacity change in the corpus, not a travelled entrance. Nothing moves. |
+| A04 | Red strike draws left to right | NO | A wipe mask along a static stroke is exact and repeatable. An I2V "draw" would invent stroke wobble and could not guarantee the final stroke matches the asset. |
+| A05 | Can appears on baseline | NO | Discrete object reveal at an exact baseline position. |
+| A06 | Four can strokes appear together | NO | They must appear as one countable group with stroke lengths identical to the mug's. Any interpolation would stagger or distort them and break the comparison. |
+| A07 | Caution mark appears | NO | One frame, no animation at all. Any I2V treatment (pulse, glow, shake) would overstate a claim the narration hedges. |
+| A08 | Patient appears | NO | Same as A03. |
+| A09 | Red strike draws left to right | NO | Same as A04, and it must be visibly the *same gesture* as A04 — only a reused asset guarantees that. |
+| A10 | Whole binary model removed | NO | An instantaneous deletion. This is the clearest `STATE_REPLACEMENT` in the video and the corpus rule is explicit: deterministic swap. An I2V dissolve would soften the exact beat that must be blunt. |
+| A11 | Left arrow draws along its curve | NO | The arrow's endpoints must land exactly on the mug and exactly on the figure's chest. I2V drift at either endpoint breaks the diagram. |
+| A12 | Single response arc appears | NO | One frame. |
+| A13 | Right arrow draws, three arcs appear | NO | The only motion in the video with a genuinely coupled two-part progression, so the closest thing to an I2V candidate. Still NO: both parts are exact-geometry diagram elements, and the three arcs must be identical in style to the left figure's single arc — the whole argument of the shot rests on the two figures differing *only* in arc count. Generation cannot guarantee that. |
+| A14 | Gauge icon + text appear | NO | One frame; text must be exact. |
+| A15 | Heart icon + text appear | NO | One frame; the heart must be the same asset drawn in SH01. |
+| A16 | Cup icon + text appear | NO | One frame; text must be exact. |
+| A17 | Factor list swaps to video card | NO | Instantaneous replacement, `STATE_REPLACEMENT` class, with Dr. Rehan required to stay bit-identical across the swap. |
+
+## Where an I2V case would have existed
+
+If this script had asked for something that plays out continuously — liquid
+pouring, a needle sweeping across a dial over time, a figure's posture
+changing — `IMAGE_TO_VIDEO_SYSTEM.md` §2 would put those in the `SEQUENTIAL`
+or `PERSISTENT_LOOP` bracket and they would be worth generating. The script
+contains no such moment. It is a sequence of statements, comparisons and
+rejections, and in this corpus's grammar those are drawn, revealed, struck out
+and replaced — not simulated.

+Is coffee good for your heart—or bad for it? Dr. Rehan says that's actually the wrong question.
+People usually ask me, then what about the energy drinks? So, energy drinks for me are much stronger than coffee and they are a bit more dangerous than coffee as well.
+So now, if the patients ask me, so is coffee good or bad for your health? I tell them that should not be the question to be asked. That's a wrong question. The real question is, how does your body respond to caffeine or coffee?
+And that's the main message: don't judge coffee only as “good” or “bad.” Dr. Rehan explains what blood pressure, heart response and quantity have to do with it in the full video. Watch it on the channel.

+# Test A — Self Audit (blind first pass)
+
+Verdicts are PASS / CONCERN / FAIL. No numerical scores. This is a
+self-assessment of a blind first pass, not a test result.
+
+---
+
+### Did I over-animate?
+**CONCERN.**
+17 motions across 33.1s ESTIMATED = 0.51 motions/sec. The frozen corpus's 8
+portrait videos measure 230 motions across 748s = 0.31 motions/sec. This plan
+is **~1.6× the corpus motion density**.
+
+Mitigating facts: every motion is the cheapest kind the corpus has (14 of 17
+are one-frame pop-ons or one-frame replacements; only 3 are drawn strokes),
+and every motion is a narration-anchored reveal that carries a distinct
+spoken concept. There is no decorative motion, no camera movement, no
+continuous animation, no loop, and no fade anywhere.
+
+Unmitigated fact: the density is above the corpus and I chose it. If the
+reviewer wants corpus-exact density, the honest cuts are A02 (fold `BAD?`
+into F01.1, revealing the whole binary at once) and A12 (fold the left
+figure's arc into A11), taking it to 15 motions / 0.45 per sec.
+
+### Did I over-reveal? (states)
+**CONCERN.**
+22 states across 33.1s = 0.67 states/sec against a corpus portrait figure of
+301 states / 748s = 0.40 states/sec — **~1.7× corpus density**.
+
+The shot-level numbers, by contrast, sit right on the corpus: 5 shots for 130
+words = 26 words/shot against a corpus range of 25–37, and a per-shot median
+of 6.6s against a corpus portrait median of 6.45s. So the shot grammar
+matches and the within-shot reveal grammar runs hot. Both facts are stated
+rather than averaged away.
+
+### Did I invent visual techniques absent from the brain?
+**PASS.**
+Every technique used appears in the corpus: one-frame pop-on reveal
+(`MASTER_MOTIONS` SPEED=INSTANT, 69 rows — the single most common value),
+progressive stroke draw (`ACTION`="ADD/DRAW", 5 rows; "Draw red strike for
+line 1/2", 5 rows), grouped simultaneous reveal ("Droplet and temperature text
+appear together"), whole-group removal/replacement (`STATE_REPLACEMENT`,
+230/438), red as a rejection/annotation accent (real in corpus), hard cuts only
+(186/186 boundaries at 0.0s), locked camera (89.8% of states).
+
+Nothing here uses a fade, dissolve, wipe transition, scale-in, slide-in,
+rotation, pulse, glow, parallax, speed ramp or camera move — all of which are
+either absent from the corpus or explicitly ruled out by
+`CAPCUT_PRODUCTION_SYSTEM.md`.
+
+### Did I create unnecessary base images?
+**CONCERN.**
+5 base images for 5 shots. Each supports 4–5 states, which is the economy the
+protocol asks for *within* a shot — but **no base image is reused across
+shots**, so cross-shot base reuse is zero.
+
+I considered and rejected two reuses: IMG01 for SH03 (rejected — SH03 needs
+two facing figures and a smaller diagram; it is a different composition, not a
+variant) and IMG02 for SH04 (rejected — no shared elements). The one genuine
+reuse opportunity I *did* take is at the asset level, not the plate level:
+O01 (mug) appears in 4 of 5 shots, C01 (Dr. Rehan) in 3, G01 (heart) in 2, G03
+(red strike) in 2, T01/T02 in 2. That matches `ASSET_DNA.md`, where reuse is
+tracked per asset and runs roughly 150/448 rows.
+
+A reviewer could reasonably argue SH01 and SH03 should share one plate. I do
+not think so, but the disagreement is legitimate and I am flagging it rather
+than burying it.
+
+### Did I map the narration concepts clearly?
+**PASS.**
+All 13 concepts named in the protocol have an explicit visual treatment:
+coffee (O01, 4 shots) · heart (G01, SH01 + SH05) · good/bad binary (SH01, SH03)
+· energy-drink comparison (SH02) · stronger stimulant (stroke counts, SH02) ·
+caution (G05, SH02) · patient question (C02, SH03) · body response (SH04) ·
+individual response (two figures, SH04) · blood pressure (SH05) · heart
+response (SH05) · quantity (SH05) · CTA (SH05 F05.4).
+
+None of them was given a redundant scene of its own — 13 concepts fit into 5
+shots.
+
+### Did I visually overstate any medical claim?
+**PASS.**
+No skull, death icon, flatline, exploding heart, heart attack, poison symbol,
+emergency-red frame, ECG or arrhythmia trace appears anywhere. No blood-pressure
+number, no caffeine milligram figure, no dose threshold, no diagnosis, no
+disease label. The gauge dial has no numbers; the quantity icon has no count.
+The energy-drink beat gets exactly one outline caution triangle, over one
+object, with nothing above the mug — the asymmetry carries "higher caution",
+which is as far as "a bit more dangerous" goes. Neither figure in SH04 is
+marked as healthy or unwell; one simply reads higher than the other. Coffee is
+never shown as universally good or universally bad — the video's own
+conclusion is that the label is the wrong tool.
+
+### Did I accidentally use external reference material?
+**PASS.**
+No xkcd or What If video, thumbnail, screenshot or storyboard was viewed,
+searched for or referenced. All visual grammar came from the frozen release's
+own files, listed in `TEST_A_MANIFEST.json`. One web search was performed, for
+medical guardrails only, restricted to heart.org / fda.gov / nih.gov /
+ncbi.nlm.nih.gov. Its output is used only to check that no visual overstates a
+claim, is labelled as a guardrail rather than a production decision wherever it
+appears, and changed no visual decision in this plan.
+
+### Did I force I2V?
+**PASS.**
+`I2V_REQUIRED = 0`. All 17 motions are CapCut. The one motion with a plausible
+case (A13, a coupled arrow-then-arcs progression) was evaluated and rejected
+on stated grounds in `I2V_DECISIONS.md`, not waved away. No AI-video use case
+was manufactured.
+
+### Can every image actually be generated?
+**CONCERN.**
+Two real risks:
+
+1. **IMG04's two identical figures.** Image models will not reliably produce
+   two figures that are pixel-identical, and the entire argument of SH04 rests
+   on them differing *only* in arc count. **Mitigation:** generate one figure
+   on transparent background, then duplicate and place it twice in the editor.
+   This is the safer build and should probably be the default.
+2. **Exact x/y percentage placement.** Every frame description in this plan
+   specifies bounding boxes to the percent, in the corpus's own convention.
+   Generators will approximate these. **Mitigation:** treat the percentages as
+   the compositing spec, not the generation spec — generate each element loose,
+   then place it to spec in the editor. All 13 overlay assets already work this
+   way; only the 5 full-frame plates depend on the generator's own layout, and
+   each of those has ≤4 elements with large empty space, which is the easiest
+   case for a generator to get roughly right.
+
+Everything else is low-risk: simple black line art on white, few elements,
+large negative space, no text requested anywhere.
+
+### Can every animation actually be executed?
+**CONCERN.**
+14 of 17 are layer visibility switches at a marked frame — trivially
+executable in any editor.
+
+The 3 drawn strokes (A04, A09, A11 and the first half of A13) need a
+progressive reveal along the stroke's own path. A04 and A09 are near-straight
+diagonals and a standard linear mask animated across the frame will do it
+correctly. **A11 and A13's arrows are curves, and CapCut's masks are linear
+and shape-based, not path-following** — a linear wipe across a curved arrow
+reveals it in a straight-edged sweep rather than along its length. Three
+fallbacks, in order of preference:
+1. Supply each arrow pre-split into 3–4 short segment PNGs and switch them on
+   in consecutive frames — reads as a draw-on, stays fully deterministic.
+2. Accept the linear wipe; on a ~0.4s reveal at phone size the difference is
+   close to invisible.
+3. Drop the draw entirely and pop the arrow on in one frame, matching the
+   other 14 motions. This is the most corpus-faithful option of the three.
+
+No animation in this plan requires a feature CapCut does not have.
+
+### Overall
+**FIRST_PASS_COMPLETE — AWAITING HUMAN REVIEW.**
+Shot grammar, transition grammar, camera grammar, motion-type grammar, asset
+grammar and text grammar all track the frozen corpus. Within-shot reveal and
+motion density run ~1.6–1.7× the corpus and cross-shot base-image reuse is
+zero — those are the two places a reviewer should push first. No claim is made
+here that the brain generalises; that is the reviewer's call after comparison.

+# Training Overlap Check
+
+```
+TRAINING_OVERLAP = NONE
+```
+
+Method: searched the frozen release's own transcript corpus only
+(`01_master_data/MASTER_SENTENCES.csv`, 604 meaningful sentences across all 14
+source videos) plus `SOURCE_VIDEO_INDEX.csv`. No internet search for matching
+content was performed, per protocol §50 and §5.
+
+## What was searched, and found
+
+| Term | Hits in the 604-sentence corpus |
+|---|---|
+| `caffeine` | 0 |
+| `energy drink` | 0 |
+| `blood pressure` | 0 |
+| `cardiac` | 0 |
+| `doctor` | 0 |
+| `patient` | 0 |
+| `coffee` | 1 |
+| `heart` | 1 |
+
+Both single hits are incidental noun co-occurrences in unrelated questions:
+
+- `weird_and_worrying_questions` S0000 — a question about chilling teeth until
+  they shatter on drinking a hot cup of coffee. The word "coffee" appears; the
+  subject is thermal fracture of enamel.
+- `what-if-earth-grew-1cm-every-second` S0086 — a sentence about hearts being
+  unable to pump blood to the brain under increased gravity. The word "heart"
+  appears; the subject is planetary growth.
+
+Neither video is about coffee, caffeine, energy drinks, blood pressure,
+cardiovascular health, medical advice, or a doctor answering a patient. No
+source video in the 14-video index is a medical or health video of any kind;
+all 14 are xkcd-style physical-hypothetical explainers.
+
+## Conclusion
+
+The supplied coffee/heart script is **not** one of the 14 training/reference
+scripts, and its subject matter, register (a doctor answering patients),
+speaker structure (attributed first-person clinical opinion) and topic domain
+(cardiovascular health) are all absent from the reference corpus. This is a
+genuine different-niche generalisation input.
+
+Two consequences worth stating plainly, since they bear on how the first pass
+should be read:
+
+1. **No medical visual precedent exists in the brain.** There is no corpus
+   evidence for how this style handles a doctor figure, a patient, a
+   consultation, a medical symbol or a caution mark. Those five decisions were
+   made by transferring the corpus's *general* grammar (minimal stick figures,
+   line-art icons, restrained accent colour, one-frame reveals) onto new
+   subjects. They are the least evidence-backed decisions in the plan and the
+   most useful ones for a reviewer to challenge.
+2. **No CTA precedent exists either.** None of the 14 source videos ends on a
+   channel call-to-action. VISUAL 05's F05.4 is therefore an extrapolation:
+   it reuses the corpus's dominant `STATE_REPLACEMENT` grammar and keeps the
+   established plate, line weight and character, but the corpus does not
+   confirm that this is how these videos would end.

+# Visual Story — Coffee / Heart Short
+
+Blind first pass. Visual grammar derived only from frozen Production
+Intelligence Brain v1.0.0. Script unchanged.
+
+## The one-line logic
+
+The video draws a model, keeps drawing it until the viewer owns it, strikes it
+out, deletes it, and replaces it with a different model. Everything else —
+the energy-drink comparison, the three factors — hangs off that single spine.
+
+## Sequence
+
+```
+BINARY MODEL DRAWN          coffee + heart, fork to GOOD? / BAD?
+DOCTOR ENTERS, STRIKES IT   same frame, one red stroke
+  ── hard cut ──
+SECOND CONTAINER APPEARS    mug vs tall unbranded can
+STRENGTH COMPARED           more stimulation marks over the can
+CAUTION ADDED               one caution mark over the can only
+  ── hard cut ──
+BINARY RETURNS              now a patient asking a doctor
+STRUCK AGAIN                one red stroke
+MODEL DELETED               fork and labels removed; the space goes empty
+  ── hard cut ──
+REPLACEMENT MODEL           coffee → arrow → person → response reading
+SECOND PERSON               same coffee, different reading
+  ── hard cut ──
+THREE FACTORS               blood pressure / heart response / quantity, one at a time
+CTA                         factor list replaced by a video card with a play mark
+```
+
+## Why this shape and not another
+
+**The binary is drawn twice on purpose.** The script rejects it twice (B02,
+B07–B08), so it has to exist on screen twice. The second occurrence is not a
+repeat of the first frame — it is re-staged as a consultation (doctor + patient)
+so the rejection lands as something said to a person, not as a slide edit.
+
+**The deletion is the hinge.** B08 removes the fork and leaves blank field.
+That empty space is the argument: the old model is gone before the new one
+arrives. The corpus's single most common motion type is `STATE_REPLACEMENT`
+(230/438, 53%) — removing and replacing illustrated content inside a locked
+frame is the grammar this corpus actually speaks.
+
+**The energy-drink section is a detour, and is staged as one.** It is the only
+place in the script where two physical objects are compared, so it gets the
+only side-by-side composition in the video. It never touches the heart, the
+doctor, or the fork — keeping it visually separate stops it contaminating the
+central message with a second argument.
+
+**The payoff is a person, not a verdict.** B09–B10 move the reading from the
+cup to the body. Two people, one coffee, two different readings — which is the
+main message stated as a picture rather than as a caption.
+
+**The CTA does not change visual language.** Same off-white field, same line
+weight, same doctor figure already on screen. Only the left-hand stack is
+swapped for a video card. There is no end-screen, no glossy panel, no motion
+the rest of the video has not already used.
+
+## Shot-to-beat map
+
+| Shot | Beats | Words | Base image | Est. duration |
+|---|---|---|---|---|
+| SH01 | B01, B02 | 1–17 | IMG01 | 4.3s ESTIMATED |
+| SH02 | B03, B04, B05 | 18–48 | IMG02 | 7.9s ESTIMATED |
+| SH03 | B06, B07, B08 | 49–80 | IMG03 | 8.1s ESTIMATED |
+| SH04 | B09, B10 | 81–106 | IMG04 | 6.6s ESTIMATED |
+| SH05 | B11, B12 | 107–130 | IMG05 | 6.1s ESTIMATED |
+
+Total 33.1s ESTIMATED (130 words ÷ 3.93 words/sec, the measured delivery rate
+of the 8 portrait videos in the frozen corpus). No measured timings exist —
+no voice track has been recorded.
+
+## Brain evidence for the overall shape
+
+- **5 shots, not 9.** The frozen corpus's 8 portrait videos run 25–37 narration
+  words per shot (407w/13, 430w/17, 510w/14, 523w/15, 333w/9). 130 words at
+  that density is 4–5 shots. The per-shot median duration that falls out
+  (6.6s) matches the portrait median of 6.45s. An earlier one-shot-per-concept
+  draft produced 9 shots at 14 words each — half the corpus's shot length —
+  and was rejected against this evidence.
+- **Content changes inside the frame, not between frames.** 522/581 states
+  (89.8%) report a LOCKED/STATIC camera (`VISUAL_DNA.md`). Every shot here is
+  a locked frame whose illustrated content is added to or replaced.
+- **Hard cuts only.** All 186 internal shot boundaries in the corpus measure a
+  0.0s gap; zero fades, dissolves or wipes exist anywhere
+  (`DECISION_RULES.md` §7). Every transition below is a hard cut.

+# Dr. Rehan — Character Master
+
+One reusable design. Draw it once, keep the file, reuse it in every shot he
+appears in. This is a recognition cue, not a likeness. Do not attempt a
+photorealistic portrait or the real person's face.
+
+**Appears in:** VISUAL 01 (SH01), VISUAL 03 (SH03), VISUAL 05 (SH05).
+
+## The design
+
+| Feature | Specification |
+|---|---|
+| Overall | Minimal stick figure, flat 2D, thin black hand-drawn linework, slightly uneven natural strokes |
+| Height in frame | Roughly 34% of frame height (y58–92%), same in all three shots |
+| Head | Plain circle outline, roughly 1/5 of total figure height |
+| Glasses | Two small rectangular lenses joined by a short bridge, across the middle of the head. Rectangular, not round — this is the primary identity cue |
+| Beard | Short solid black filled arc under the chin. Small. Not a full beard shape |
+| Hair | One short curved side-swept stroke across the top of the head |
+| Face | Nothing else. No eyes, no mouth, no nose, no ears |
+| Body | Single straight stroke |
+| Arms | Two simple straight strokes |
+| Legs | Two simple straight strokes |
+| Line weight | Identical to every other line in the project — one uniform fine-marker weight |
+| Colour | None. Pure black line |
+| Doctor cue | The glasses + beard combination only. **No coat, no stethoscope, no clipboard, no badge** |
+
+## The three poses needed
+
+| Pose | Used in | Difference |
+|---|---|---|
+| **A — arm raised** | VISUAL 01, x8–30% y70–95% | Faces right. Near arm raised at ~45° pointing up-right toward the diagram. Far arm hangs |
+| **B — arms down, facing right** | VISUAL 03, x6–28% y58–92% (baked into IMG03) | Faces right. Both arms hang at sides |
+| **C — arms down, facing left** | VISUAL 05, x66–92% y58–92% (baked into IMG05) | Faces left. Both arms hang at sides. Mirror of B |
+
+Pose A is a standalone transparent PNG (asset C01). Poses B and C are drawn
+inside base plates IMG03 and IMG05.
+
+**Consistency method:** draw pose A once as a transparent PNG. Generate IMG03
+and IMG05 with the figure description copied word for word from the table
+above. Then compare the three side by side before building — head size,
+glasses width and beard size must match. If one drifts, regenerate that plate.
+
+## Why he is not a doctor cliché
+
+The corpus has no medical video and no doctor asset. A white coat and
+stethoscope would be an import from stock medical illustration, not a transfer
+from the learned grammar. The narration names him; the glasses and beard make
+him the one distinguishable person on screen. That is all the identity the
+plan needs, and it is why the patient (C02) and the two figures in VISUAL 04
+(C03) are deliberately featureless.
+
+## The other people in this video
+
+| Asset | Who | Design |
+|---|---|---|
+| **C02** | The patient, VISUAL 03 | Plain stick figure. Round head, **no face at all** — no glasses, no beard, no hair, no features. Near arm slightly raised as if asking. Faces left |
+| **C03** | The two comparison people, VISUAL 04 | Plain stick figure, round head, no face, no features, neutral forward-facing posture, arms at sides. **Generate ONE. Duplicate the layer in CapCut for the second.** Never generate two |
+
+C03's rule is not a preference. The whole argument of VISUAL 04 is *same
+coffee, same arrow, different response* — if the two figures differ in any
+visible way, the viewer reads the difference as the explanation. Duplication
+guarantees they are identical. Generation does not.

+## Rules
+
+| Rule | Why |
+|---|---|
+| Never generated in an image | Generators misrender short words, and each of these must be removable as its own layer |
+| Text matches the narration word for word | `BLOOD PRESSURE`, `HEART RESPONSE`, `QUANTITY` are spoken terms; a misrendered medical term is a factual error |
+| No numbers anywhere | No mmHg, no milligrams, no millilitres, no cup counts, no thresholds. The narration supplies none |
+| Appears on the word onset | Same rule as every other reveal: no offset padding |
+| Icon and label never stagger | T04 and T05 appear in the same frame as their icons — they are one unit |

+1. **Grammar.** Nothing resembling an instrument dial exists among the 448
+   catalogued corpus assets. It is not a transfer from the learned style; it is
+   an import from generic infographic design.
+2. **Medical accuracy.** A needle resting somewhere on a dial reads as a
+   *reading*. A tick mark on the rim reads as a *threshold*. The narration
+   supplies neither. Directional replacements were considered and rejected for
+   the same reason — an up-arrow next to BLOOD PRESSURE would assert that
+   coffee raises it, which this script never says.
+
+The text is not a weak cue here: it lands on the word, inside a plate the
+viewer has already been shown, alongside two plates that do carry icons, so
+the list structure does the work an icon would otherwise do. Because the text
+now owns the whole plate, **set it larger than it would have been** beside an
+icon.
+
+**One thing to verify on a real phone, not a desktop preview:** the estimated
+hold for `BLOOD PRESSURE` is ~0.5s before the next plate fills. That is the
+tightest reading demand in the plan. If the recorded narration is faster than
+estimated and 14 characters cannot be read in time, the fix is a type-size or
+hold change — **not** a new icon.

+---

+# MEDICAL GUARDRAILS — fixed, do not relax during production
+
+The video's whole visual argument is:

+Nothing in the visuals may strengthen a claim the narration does not make.

+|---|---|
+| Stimulation strokes (2 for coffee, 4 for the can) | Exploding heart, skull, death imagery |
+| One small muted-red caution triangle over the can | Flatlines, ECG tracings, hospital or emergency imagery |
+| Unlabelled red response arcs, counted not measured | Numbers, scales, units, mmHg, milligrams, millilitres |
+| Three cups in decreasing size for "quantity" | Dose figures, safe-limit marks, thresholds |
+| The text BLOOD PRESSURE, alone | Gauges, dials, needles, meters, up/down arrows |
+
+Coffee is never drawn as universally healthy and never as universally
+dangerous. The energy drink is never a real product — no logo, no brand name,
+no lettering, no brand colours.
+
+---
+
+# FINAL SANITY CHECK
+
+| Check | Result |
+|---|---|
+| Every line of narration covered | **YES** — w1–w130 across 5 visuals, no gap, no overlap |
+| Every visual has a base image | **YES** — IMG01–IMG05, one per visual |

+| Camera movement added | **NO** — 0 |
+| Fades added | **NO** — 0. Four butt cuts |
+| Script wording changed | **NO** — 130 words verbatim |
+| States or motions added or removed vs Revision 1 | **NO** — 20 and 15, identical |
+
+**Known risks carried over from Revision 1, unresolved by design:**
+
+1. All durations are ESTIMATED from 3.93 words/sec. Every operation anchors to
+   a word, so nothing breaks — but recompute pacing against the real audio

+2. VISUAL 01 and VISUAL 05 reveal faster than the corpus's 90th percentile.

+# Executability Check — Revision 1
+
+Every operation in the revised plan, tested against one question: **can the
+named tool produce exactly this, repeatably, without a lucky generation?**
+
+## Summary
+
+| | First pass | Revision 1 |
+|---|---|---|
+| Operations with no deterministic implementation | 2 (A11, A13 curved draws) | **0** |
+| Operations relying on a lucky generation | 1 (IMG04's two identical figures) | **0** |
+| Operations needing a documented workaround | 2 (SH03 / SH05 partial plate removal, undocumented in the first pass) | 2, **now documented** |
+| Motions requiring image-to-video generation | 0 | 0 |
+
+## Resolved
+
+**1. Curved arrow draws (was A11, A13).** CapCut's masks are linear and
+shape-based; they do not follow an arbitrary path. A curved stroke revealing
+itself along its own curve therefore had no exact implementation, and the first
+pass named three fallbacks without choosing one. Resolved by looking up what
+the corpus actually does with curved arrows — *"Reveal the six red curved arrow
+strokes toward the book pages"*, 0.292s / 7 frames, a group reveal — and
+adopting that. The arrows now appear whole in one frame (M10, M11). The
+corpus-faithful answer and the buildable answer were the same answer.
+
+**2. Two pixel-identical figures (IMG04).** The first-pass prompt asked an
+image model for "two stick figures that are completely identical to each
+other", and the entire shot's argument — same coffee, same arrows, only the
+arc count differs — fails if they differ at all. Resolved by removing the
+figures from the base plate: C03 is generated once as a transparent PNG and the
+layer is duplicated in the editor with a changed X position. Identity is now
+structural rather than hoped for.
+
+**3. Strike stroke timing (was A04, A09).** Not an executability problem but a
+pacing one: a wipe mask animated across half a second is trivially buildable
+and wrong. Retimed to 4 frames on measured corpus durations (0.125–0.208s).
+
+## Still requires a workaround — now written down
+
+**Partial removal from a shared base plate (SH03 and SH05).** In both shots the
+doctor and a removable group are drawn in the same base image, but only the
+group is removed. A single opacity switch would take the doctor with it.
+
+Fix, specified in `REVISED_CAPCUT_BUILD.md`: export each of those two base
+images as two files at the same canvas size — a base carrying the off-white
+field and the doctor, and a transparent-background file carrying just the
+removable group. Switch off only the group.
+
+This is not a compromise. It is what the asset spec already implies by calling
+G06 and G09 single removable groups, and the first pass simply never said how
+to build it. Cost: two extra exports and two extra layers.
+
+## Verified buildable as specified
+
+| Operation class | Count | Tool mechanism |
+|---|---|---|
+| Layer / group visibility on at a frame | 10 | Opacity or visibility switch |
+| Group visibility off at a frame | 1 | Same |
+| Simultaneous off + on at one frame | 1 | Two switches on the same frame |
+| Coupled multi-layer reveal at one frame | 5 | Grouped layers, one switch |
+| Linear wipe mask, 4 frames | 1 | Standard linear mask animation |
+| Native text layers | 6 | Editor text |
+| Butt cuts between shots | 4 | No transition effect applied |
+| Camera moves | 0 | — |
+| Generated video clips | 0 | — |
+
+(Counts overlap because coupled reveals are also visibility switches.)
+
+## Residual risks — no fix applied, stated for the reviewer
+
+1. **All timings are ESTIMATED.** Every duration in this plan derives from
+   3.93 words/sec, the measured portrait-subcorpus rate. Real narration will
+   differ, and a slower hook in particular would relieve SH01's density.
+   Nothing in the plan depends on the estimate being right — every operation is
+   anchored to a word onset, not to a clock time — but the per-shot density
+   figures in `REVISED_SHOT_PLAN.csv` will move once the audio exists. They
+   must be recomputed against the real track before anyone judges pacing.
+
+2. **SH01 and SH05 exceed the corpus's 90th-percentile reveal rate.** SH01 runs
+   an estimated 1.16 states/sec and SH05 0.82, against a portrait p90 of 0.67.
+   Both are driven by the script's own word density — SH01 names four concepts
+   in 17 words, SH05 names three in six — not by added decoration. No cut was
+   made for this, because every state in both shots fires on a distinct concept
+   word. This is the single most likely thing a human reviewer will disagree
+   with, and the disagreement would be reasonable.
+
+3. **Hand-drawn consistency across five separately generated plates.** The five
+   base images are generated independently and must share line weight, stroke
+   character and off-white value. Generation variance is a real risk that no
+   prompt wording fully removes. Mitigation, unapplied: generate all five in
+   one session with a fixed seed where the tool allows, and re-generate the
+   whole set rather than one plate if any drifts.
+
+4. **The mug appears at four different scales** (IMG01 large, IMG02 standing,

+# Release Metadata Issue — v1.0.0
+
+**Recorded, not fixed.** Per instruction, v1.0.0 was not altered during this
+review. This is a release-maintenance item for a separate patch release; it
+must not be bundled with Test A work.
+
+## The inconsistency
+
+`releases/production_intelligence_brain-v1.0.0/BRAIN_MANIFEST.json`:
+
+```
+project_status    = "COMPLETE_VALIDATED"
+release_status    = "PREPARING"
+release_frozen_at = null
+```
+
+The Test A protocol expected `STATUS = COMPLETE_VALIDATED / FROZEN`. The
+release therefore describes itself as still being prepared while being used,
+and published by hash, as a frozen artefact.
+
+## Why the first pass proceeded, and why this revision did too
+
+Everything except the two string fields indicates a frozen, validated release:
+
+- `validator/validate_brain.py` returns `RESULT: PASS` with zero failures. Run
+  before and after the first pass, and again after this revision.
+- Every declared count matches the protocol exactly: 7864 words, 604 sentences,
+  200 shots, 581 states, 438 motions, 448 assets, 1421 A/V events
+  (581 STATE_CHANGE + 438 MOTION_START + 402 MOTION_END).
+- `RELEASE_MANIFEST.json` declares 50 files with zero hash or size mismatches.
+- The distributed ZIP is sealed by a published SHA-256:
+  `05e3277199efc1a8e780db87b9e25f9e294496091be45d2d0f36afe760539270`.
+
+A published archive hash is a stronger freeze guarantee than a status string,
+so the release was treated as **frozen-by-hash**. No test stop was triggered.
+The first pass recorded this in `TEST_A_MANIFEST.json.brain_status_note`.
+
+## What a fix would involve — for a future v1.0.1, not now
+
+1. Set `release_status` to `FROZEN` and `release_frozen_at` to the real freeze
+   timestamp.
+2. Re-hash `BRAIN_MANIFEST.json` and update its entry in
+   `RELEASE_MANIFEST.json`.
+3. Re-build and re-hash the distribution ZIP, publishing a new
+   `.sha256` alongside it.
+4. Re-run `validator/validate_brain.py` and record the result.
+5. Release as **v1.0.1**, leaving v1.0.0 and its published hash intact so that
+   Test A's first pass and this revision remain reproducible against the exact
+   artefact they were run on.
+
+## Scope boundary
+
+Do not perform steps 1–5 as part of Test A. Changing v1.0.0's bytes would
+invalidate the provenance of both the blind first pass and this revision.
+Re-running Test A against a patched v1.0.1 is a separate decision, and if it is
+taken, the blind pass cannot be re-run blind.

+# Revised Animation Prompts — Revision 1
+
+One prompt per motion, 1–3 lines each. Every prompt names what moves, what
+stays static, and states that the camera does not move.
+
+**15 motions. 14 are one-frame appearances or removals. 1 is a 4-frame draw.
+All 15 are built in the editor. None requires image-to-video generation.**
+
+That ratio is not a stylistic choice — it is what the portrait corpus does. In
+the brain's 230 portrait motions, the single most common SPEED value is
+`ONE-FRAME CHANGE` (28 rows), followed by `FAST` (27) and `INSTANT` (21), and a
+further 30 rows give an explicit frame count between 3 and 15 frames.
+
+## Changes from the first pass
+
+| First pass | Revision 1 |
+|---|---|
+| A04 strike draws across "wrong … question." | **M04** draws in 4 frames on "wrong" |
+| A09 second strike draws across "not … asked." | **Removed entirely** |
+| A10 deletion on "That's" (w77) | **M09** deletion on "not" (w70) |
+| A11 left arrow draws along a curve, then A12 pops the arc | **M10** — arrow and arc pop together in one frame |
+| A13 right arrow draws along a curve, then arcs pop | **M11** — arrow and all three arcs pop together in one frame |
+| A14 reveals gauge icon + text | **M12** reveals text only |
+
+The three curved draws are gone. Every one of them was replaced by the
+treatment the corpus actually uses for curved arrows — a group reveal in a
+handful of frames — which happens to also be the only treatment CapCut can
+execute exactly.
+
+---
+
+## SH01
+
+**M01** — On the onset of the word "good", the two fork lines, the left label
+plate and its GOOD? text appear together in a single frame. The off-white
+field, the coffee mug and the heart do not change. No camera movement.
+
+**M02** — On the onset of the word "bad", the right label plate and its BAD?
+text appear together in a single frame. The mug, the heart, the fork lines and
+the left plate with its text all stay exactly where they are. No camera
+movement.
+
+**M03** — On the onset of the word "Rehan", the doctor figure appears in the
+lower-left field in a single frame. He does not walk in, slide in or scale up;
+he is simply there on the next frame. The mug, heart, fork and both plates with
+their text are unchanged. No camera movement.
+
+**M04** — On the onset of the word "wrong", the muted-red strike stroke draws
+itself left to right along its own fixed diagonal path, completing in 4 frames.
+The mug, heart, fork lines, both plates, both text labels and the doctor are
+all completely static throughout. No camera movement. The stroke must be
+finished well before the word "question."
+
+---
+
+## SH02
+
+**M05** — On the onset of the word "energy", the tall unbranded can appears
+standing on the baseline to the right of the mug, in a single frame. It does
+not drop in, bounce or scale. The baseline, the mug and the mug's two strokes
+are unchanged. No camera movement.
+
+**M06** — On the onset of the word "stronger", all four of the can's
+stimulation strokes appear together in one frame as a single group. They must
+not stagger or appear one by one. The baseline, mug, the mug's two strokes and
+the can are unchanged. No camera movement.
+
+**M07** — On the onset of the word "dangerous", the muted-red caution triangle
+appears above the can's strokes in a single frame. It does not pulse, flash,
+shake, glow or grow, and nothing else in the frame reacts to it. The baseline,
+both containers and both stroke groups are unchanged. No camera movement.
+
+---
+
+## SH03
+
+**M08** — On the onset of the word "patients", the patient figure appears in
+the empty right field, facing the doctor, in a single frame. The doctor, the
+compact binary diagram and both text labels are unchanged. No camera movement.
+Hold this frame, completely still, for the whole of the patient's question —
+roughly 4.3 seconds ESTIMATED. Nothing moves during that hold.
+
+**M09** — On the onset of the word "not", the whole binary diagram group — the
+small mug, both branch lines, both label plates and both text labels —
+disappears in a single frame, leaving empty off-white. There is no fade, no
+wipe and no shrink. The doctor and the patient do not move at all and remain
+facing each other. No camera movement. Hold the emptied frame for the rest of
+the sentence and through "That's a wrong question."
+
+---
+
+## SH04
+
+**M10** — On the onset of the word "respond", the left connector arrow and the
+left figure's single red arc appear together in one frame. The arrow is a
+complete curved stroke that appears whole; it does not draw itself along its
+path. The mug, the baseline and both figures are unchanged. No camera movement.
+
+**M11** — On the onset of the word "judge", the right connector arrow and all
+three of the right figure's red arcs appear together in one frame. The arrow
+appears whole, and the three arcs appear as one group, not one at a time. The
+mug, the baseline, both figures, the left arrow and the left arc are unchanged.
+No camera movement. Hold through "or 'bad.'"
+
+---
+
+## SH05
+
+**M12** — On the onset of the word "blood", the text BLOOD PRESSURE appears
+inside the top list plate in a single frame. No icon appears with it. The
+doctor, all three plates and the connector line are unchanged, and the middle
+and bottom plates stay empty. No camera movement.
+
+**M13** — On the onset of the word "heart", the small heart icon and the text
+HEART RESPONSE appear together inside the middle plate in one frame. They must
+not stagger. The doctor, all three plates, the connector line and the top
+plate's text are unchanged, and the bottom plate stays empty. No camera
+movement.
+
+**M14** — On the onset of the word "quantity", the three-cup icon and the text
+QUANTITY appear together inside the bottom plate in one frame. The doctor, all
+three plates, the connector line and the contents of the top two plates are
+unchanged. No camera movement.

+**M15** — On the onset of the word "full", the three plates, all of their
+contents and the connector line disappear, and in the same single frame the
+video card, its hollow play triangle and the text WATCH THE FULL VIDEO appear
+in their place. It is one simultaneous swap, not a removal followed by a
+reveal. The off-white field and Dr. Rehan do not change at all. No camera

+
+## Motions that were considered and deliberately not written
+
+- No camera move anywhere. Not a slow push, not a Ken Burns drift, not a
+  parallax, not a settle. Every well-formed `CAMERA_STATE` row in the brain's
+  581 states is in the LOCKED/STATIC family.
+- No fade or dissolve anywhere, including on the deletion at M09, where the
+  instinct to soften is strongest. The corpus has zero fades across 186
+  measured shot boundaries.
+- No pulse, beat or throb on the heart, and no motion at all on the response

+  not describe; animated arcs would imply a live measurement.
+- No animation on the caution triangle. The narration hedges ("a bit more
+  dangerous"), so the visual hedges too.
+- No entrance movement for any character. The corpus never travels a character
+  into frame.
