+#!/usr/bin/env python3
+"""Self-contained validator for weird_and_worrying_questions.
+Run: python3 00_source/verify.py   (from this video's project root)
+Stdlib only. Prints PASS or raises AssertionError on the first failure.
+"""
+import csv
+import json
+import re
+from pathlib import Path
+
+ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parent.parent
+
+def read_csv(name):
+    with open(ROOT / "02_analysis" / name, newline="") as f:
+        return list(csv.DictReader(f))
+
+def read_text(rel):
+    return (ROOT / rel).read_text()
+
+# ---- Timeline coverage ----
+timeline = read_csv("TIMELINE.csv")
+assert len(timeline) == 27, f"expected 27 states, got {len(timeline)}"
+rows = sorted(timeline, key=lambda r: int(r["IN"]))
+expected_in = 0
+total_frames = 0
+for r in rows:
+    in_f, out_f = int(r["IN"]), int(r["OUT"])
+    assert in_f == expected_in, f"gap/overlap before state {r['STATE_ID']}: expected IN={expected_in}, got {in_f}"
+    assert out_f >= in_f, f"invalid range in state {r['STATE_ID']}"
+    dur_frames = int(r["DURATION"].split("/")[0])
+    assert dur_frames == out_f - in_f + 1, f"duration mismatch in state {r['STATE_ID']}"
+    expected_in = out_f + 1
+    total_frames += dur_frames
+assert total_frames == 1139, f"total frames {total_frames} != 1139"
+assert rows[-1]["OUT"] == "1138", "timeline does not reach the last frame (1138)"
+
+shots = sorted(set(r["SHOT_ID"] for r in timeline))
+assert shots == ["S01"], f"unexpected shot set: {shots} (this video is a single locked-camera shot)"
+
+# ---- Asset manifest ----
+assets = read_csv("ASSET_MANIFEST.csv")
+assert len(assets) == 19, f"expected 19 assets, got {len(assets)}"
+asset_ids = set(a["ASSET_ID"] for a in assets)
+assert len(asset_ids) == 19, "duplicate ASSET_ID found"
+
+def split_ids(s):
+    return [x.strip() for x in s.split(";") if x.strip()]
+
+referenced_assets = set()
+for r in timeline:
+    referenced_assets |= set(split_ids(r["ASSET_IDS"]))
+missing = referenced_assets - asset_ids
+assert not missing, f"TIMELINE references unknown asset IDs: {missing}"
+unused = asset_ids - referenced_assets
+assert unused <= {"AU01"}, f"unexpected unused assets (only AU01 should be timeline-unreferenced): {unused}"
+
+# ---- Motion events ----
+motions = read_csv("MOTION_EVENTS.csv")
+assert len(motions) == 25, f"expected 25 motion events, got {len(motions)}"
+motion_ids = set(m["MOTION_ID"] for m in motions)
+assert motion_ids == {f"A{n:02d}" for n in range(1, 26)}, f"unexpected motion ID set: {sorted(motion_ids)}"
+for m in motions:
+    assert m["SHOT_ID"] in shots, f"motion {m['MOTION_ID']} references unknown shot {m['SHOT_ID']}"
+    assert int(m["OUT"]) >= int(m["IN"]), f"motion {m['MOTION_ID']} has invalid IN/OUT"
+
+referenced_motions = set()
+for r in timeline:
+    for mid in split_ids(r["MOTION_IDS"]):
+        if mid.startswith("A") and mid[1:].isdigit():
+            referenced_motions.add(mid)
+missing_m = referenced_motions - motion_ids
+assert not missing_m, f"TIMELINE references unknown motion IDs: {missing_m}"
+assert referenced_motions == motion_ids, f"not every motion is referenced from TIMELINE: unreferenced={motion_ids - referenced_motions}"
+
+# ---- CapCut guide ----
+capcut = read_text("03_capcut/CAPCUT_REBUILD.md")
+for s in shots:
+    assert re.search(rf"^## {s} ", capcut, re.M), f"CAPCUT_REBUILD.md missing header for {s}"
+for mid in sorted(motion_ids):
+    assert mid in capcut, f"CAPCUT_REBUILD.md never references motion {mid}"
+
+# ---- Image prompts ----
+img_prompts = read_text("04_image_to_video/IMAGE_PROMPTS.md")
+img_headers = re.findall(r"^## (IMG\d+)$", img_prompts, re.M)
+assert len(img_headers) == 14, f"expected 14 IMG headers, got {len(img_headers)}"
+assert img_headers == [f"IMG{n:02d}" for n in range(1, 15)], f"unexpected/non-sequential IMG headers: {img_headers}"
+baked_yes = len(re.findall(r"^TEXT BAKED: YES", img_prompts, re.M))
+baked_no = len(re.findall(r"^TEXT BAKED: NO", img_prompts, re.M))
+assert baked_yes == 1, f"expected exactly 1 TEXT BAKED: YES (the plaque heading), got {baked_yes}"
+assert baked_no == 13, f"expected exactly 13 TEXT BAKED: NO, got {baked_no}"
+
+# ---- Animation prompts ----
+anim = read_text("04_image_to_video/ANIMATION_PROMPTS.md")
+anim_headers = re.findall(r"^## (A\d+)$", anim, re.M)
+assert set(anim_headers) == motion_ids, f"ANIMATION_PROMPTS.md headers {sorted(anim_headers)} != motion set {sorted(motion_ids)}"
+for block in re.split(r"^## A\d+$", anim, flags=re.M)[1:]:
+    m = re.search(r"ANIMATION PROMPT:\s*(.+?)(?:\n##|\Z)", block, re.S)
+    assert m, "a motion block is missing its ANIMATION PROMPT line"
+    prompt_text = m.group(1).strip()
+    assert 1 <= len(prompt_text) <= 500, f"animation prompt out of 1-500 char range ({len(prompt_text)} chars)"
+
+# ---- I2V guide ----
+i2v = read_text("04_image_to_video/I2V_REBUILD.md")
+for s in shots:
+    assert re.search(rf"^## {s} ", i2v, re.M), f"I2V_REBUILD.md missing header for {s}"
+
+# ---- Audio map sanity ----
+audio_map = read_text("05_audio/AUDIO_MAP.md")
+assert "UNAVAILABLE" in audio_map, "AUDIO_MAP.md should record that transcript is unavailable"
+assert "45.468" in audio_map, "AUDIO_MAP.md missing a measured silence gap"
+
+# ---- Cross-project markdown link check ----
+link_re = re.compile(r"\[[^\]]*\]\(([^)]+)\)")
+for md_file in ROOT.rglob("*.md"):
+    text = md_file.read_text(errors="ignore")
+    for target in link_re.findall(text):
+        if target.startswith("http") or target.startswith("#"):
+            continue
+        target_path = (md_file.parent / target.split("#")[0]).resolve()
+        assert target_path.exists(), f"{md_file.relative_to(ROOT)} has a broken link to {target}"
+
+# ---- RUN_STATE.json counts (if present and populated) ----
+run_state_path = ROOT / "RUN_STATE.json"
+if run_state_path.exists():
+    run_state = json.loads(run_state_path.read_text())
+    counts = run_state.get("counts")
+    if counts:
+        assert counts["shots"] == 1
+        assert counts["visual_states"] == 27
+        assert counts["unique_assets"] == 19
+        assert counts["motion_events"] == 25
+        assert counts["unique_images"] == 14
+
+print("PASS: timeline coverage, asset/motion ID cross-refs, CapCut shot+motion coverage, "
+      "image/animation prompt counts and length limits, I2V shot coverage, audio map sanity, "
+      "and file links.")

+# Visual DNA — weird_and_worrying_questions
+
+Global, evidence-supported production characteristics. Scene-specific detail lives in `TIMELINE.csv`; this file states the repeated rule once and notes exceptions.
+
+## CHARACTER DNA
+Repeated rule: a single plain bald stick figure (C01) — round head, minimal limbs, no facial features beyond an implied gaze — seated at a desk for the entire video; this is the sole recurring "on-camera" character.
+Exceptions: C02 (hat + trenchcoat + magnifying glass) appears once, single-use, for the "mirrors" aside (F01.8) and never recurs. A second, distinct illustrated stick figure (G06, the "imagined self" inside the thought bubble) and a crying figure (G11) are graphic elements, not the on-camera character C01.
+
+## ENVIRONMENT DNA
+Repeated rule: flat plain white background (E01) for the entire runtime; no set dressing beyond the desk.
+Exceptions: none observed.
+
+## OBJECT DNA
+Repeated rule: the desk + monitor + keyboard (O01) is a fixed, static prop present and unmoving in every state.
+Exceptions: a physical coffee mug (O02) is held by C01 only in the opening joke (F01.0–F01.5) and is thrown off-panel during F01.6; it never reappears.
+
+## COLOR PALETTE
+Repeated rule: pure black line-art on white, matching a hand-drawn/xkcd-style aesthetic; the only non-monochrome element is the red mercury column inside the thermometer (G03).
+Exceptions: none.
+
+## LIGHTING
+Repeated rule: flat, shadowless line-art; no lighting model present.
+
+## CAMERA / FRAMING
+Repeated rule: **one fixed, locked camera position for the entire video** — no cuts, pans, zooms, or reframing were observed anywhere. This is the video's defining structural trait and is why the whole runtime is modeled as a single shot (S01). All apparent "cuts" from scene-cut detection are large content swaps within this one static frame (thought-bubble graphics appearing/clearing, a second character entering/exiting), not camera changes.
+Exceptions: none.
+
+## COMPOSITION
+Repeated rule: C01 + desk occupy the lower-right area of frame; a gray question card (T01), when present, sits top-left; the thought bubble (G01), when present, occupies the upper-center/upper-left area above C01.
+Exceptions: the two "plaque" states (F01.21–F01.22) replace the Q-card + bubble layout with a single full-frame graphic (G10); the closing caption states (F01.25–F01.26) show no bubble or Q-card at all, only a short caption line above C01.
+
+## TYPOGRAPHY
+Repeated rule: two distinct text systems are used consistently — T01 (a gray rounded-rectangle "Q" card with sentence-case question body text and a "— Name" attribution line, used for all five named questions) and T02 (bold, all-caps, hand-drawn-style caption text with occasional underline emphasis, used for asides/punchlines/reactions that are not attributed questions).
+Exceptions: none.
+
+## GRAPHICS
+Repeated rule: every gag illustration (teeth, thermometer, mirror/star array, volcano, reactor, plaque, crying figure) is a bespoke single-use graphic drawn inside or replacing the thought bubble; none are reused across different jokes.
+Exceptions: the thought-bubble container outline itself (G01) is the one recurring graphic, reused as a frame for five of the six gags.
+
+## ILLUSTRATION / 3D STYLE
+Repeated rule: loose hand-drawn black-ink vector/sketch style, consistent with the same illustration language used elsewhere in this project (matches `what_if_the_moon_were_made_of_protons` and `how_long_could_you_drive_towards_the_sunset`).
+
+## DEPTH
+Repeated rule: flat 2D compositing throughout; no foreground/midground/background layering beyond the character+desk vs. bubble-content plane.
+
+## MOTION LANGUAGE
+Repeated rule: nearly every state transition is a **content swap** (a graphic or caption appears, fully formed, or clears to blank) rather than a continuous physical animation; genuine continuous motion is limited to two cases — the thermometer's mercury drop (A03) and the crying figure's growing puddle (A23). No camera movement, parallax, particles, or decorative motion of any kind was observed anywhere.
+Exceptions: the mug-throw (A06) is the one instance of an object undergoing a translating motion (off-panel).
+
+## TRANSITION LANGUAGE
+Repeated rule: all transitions between visual states are hard content cuts/fades within the single locked frame (bubble/Q-card content appears or clears); there are no wipes, dissolves, or camera-driven transitions.
+
+## ASSET REUSE PATTERN
+Repeated rule: this video has the lowest reuse profile of any video in this project — of 19 total assets, only C01, E01, O01, G01, T01, T02 and AU01 (7 of 19) recur across multiple states; the remaining 12 assets (C02, O02, G02–G11 minus G01) are single-use, one per gag, reflecting the video's fast joke-per-question structure (six independent question/answer gags in ~47 seconds).

+# Visual DNA
+
+## Observed global rules
+
+- Hand-drawn, thin black line illustration on near-white field; gray pencil-like hatching fills Earth, objects, and shadows.
+- Stick-figure presenter/people recur. Geometry is flat, centered or side-by-side, with broad empty space.
+- Time labels occupy a black strip at top on many explanatory scenes: `T = ...` in small white uppercase text.
+- Important numerical change uses red handwritten-style text, red underline, or red arrow. Most explanatory text is black uppercase hand lettering.
+- Camera is normally locked, full-frame 16:9. Major changes are hard cuts; whiteboard composition is reused. No observed decorative parallax, bloom, particles, or continuous camera drift.
+- Motion language is sparse: draw-on/reveal, object/graphic replacement, simple translation, scale change, sequential collapse, and occasional diagram line growth. Static holds are common.
+
+## Exceptions
+
+- S02 and S39 use flat red branded title/end cards with black illustration and white text.
+- S37–S38 use a black space field, grayscale Earth/Moon, thin orbit lines, and white satellite drawings.
+- S03 briefly uses a dark cave/opening inside a whiteboard drawing.
+
+## Reconstruction consequence
+
+Keep backgrounds locked. Build exact text as editor overlays, not generated-image text. Treat source-specific artwork, fonts, music, editor, model, lens, and stock source as UNKNOWN.

+[00.000–02.000]
+
+"This question comes from Dennis, who asks,"
+
+[02.420–04.500]
+
+"how long would it take for people to notice their weight gain"
+
+[04.500–08.040]
+
+"if the mean radius of the world increased by one centimeter every second,"
+
+[08.440–10.400]
+
+"assuming the average composition of rock were maintained?"
+
+[12.480–14.760]
+
+"Let's imagine the whole Earth from crust to core"
+
+[14.760–18.460]
+
+"starts expanding uniformly beneath our human structures which don't expand."
+
+[18.940–22.200]
+
+"To avoid another drain, the ocean scenario will assume the ocean expands to."
+
+[22.680–25.260]
+
+"When the Earth started expanding, you'd feel a slight jolt,"
+
+[25.540–28.040]
+
+"and then you'd be moving steadily upward at one centimeter per second"
+
+[28.040–30.060]
+
+"and wouldn't feel any kind of ongoing acceleration."
+
+[30.500–32.540]
+
+"For the rest of the day, you wouldn't notice much of anything."
+
+[33.020–36.400]
+
+"After the first day, the Earth would have expanded by 864 meters."
+
+[36.880–39.280]
+
+"Gravity would take a long time to increase noticeably."
+
+[39.640–41.840]
+
+"If you weighed 70 kilograms when the expansion started,"
+
+[42.140–44.700]
+
+"you'd weigh 70.01 at the end of the first day."
+
+[45.200–48.520]
+
+"With the ground expanding beneath them, how fast would our roads and bridges fail?"
+
+[49.060–50.560]
+
+"Well, not as quickly as you might think."
+
+[50.900–51.980]
+
+"Here's a puzzle I heard once."
+
+[52.320–54.140]
+
+"Imagine you tied a rope tightly around the Earth,"
+
+[54.320–56.020]
+
+"so it was hugging the surface all the way around."
+
+[56.020–58.760]
+
+"Now imagine you wanted to raise the rope one meter off the ground."
+
+[59.180–61.140]
+
+"How much extra length would you need to add to the rope?"
+
+[61.580–62.720]
+
+"Miles? Hundreds of miles?"
+
+[63.260–64.940]
+
+"The answer's about six meters."
+
+[65.400–66.960]
+
+"Circumference is proportional to radius,"
+
+[67.180–68.860]
+
+"so if you increase the radius by one unit,"
+
+[69.100–71.100]
+
+"you increase the circumference by two pi units."
+
+[71.700–74.500]
+
+"After one day, the 40,000 kilometer circumference of the Earth"
+
+[74.500–77.200]
+
+"would increase by two pi times 864 meters,"
+
+[77.400–80.540]
+
+"or 5.4 kilometers, which is about 0.01 percent."
+
+[80.880–82.980]
+
+"And that'd be handled easily by virtually all structures."
+
+[83.320–85.700]
+
+"Concrete expanding attracts by more than that every day."
+
+[86.020–90.060]
+
+"One of the first real effects you'd notice would be that GPS satellites would stop working correctly."
+
+[90.420–92.280]
+
+"The satellites would stay and roughly the same orbits,"
+
+[92.560–96.560]
+
+"but the incredibly precise timing and synchronization between ground stations and satellites would"
+
+[96.560–99.780]
+
+"be ruined within hours. Most other clocks would keep working fine."
+
+[100.120–102.480]
+
+"However, if you have a very precise pendulum clock,"
+
+[102.740–103.980]
+
+"you might notice something odd."
+
+[104.300–107.220]
+
+"By the end of the day, it would be three seconds ahead of where it should be."
+
+[107.560–110.680]
+
+"After a month, the Earth would have expanded by 26 kilometers,"
+
+[110.920–112.480]
+
+"an increase of 0.4 percent."
+
+[112.480–115.960]
+
+"Surface gravity would also only have gone up 0.4 percent,"
+
+[116.040–118.960]
+
+"even though the Earth's mass would have increased by 1.2 percent."
+
+[119.280–120.940]
+
+"Surface gravity is proportional to radius,"
+
+[121.260–123.840]
+
+"which is because as the planet grows, it gets more massive,"
+
+[124.100–126.040]
+
+"but you also get further away from the middle."
+
+[126.460–128.800]
+
+"You wouldn't notice this difference in weight even using a scale."
+
+[129.200–132.840]
+
+"Human body weights vary by much more than 0.4 percent over the course of a day,"
+
+[133.060–136.780]
+
+"let alone a month, and gravity itself varies by this much between different cities."
+
+[137.220–138.820]
+
+"What you would notice is the expansion."
+
+[139.300–141.800]
+
+"You'd see lots of cracks opening up in long concrete structures"
+
+[141.800–143.940]
+
+"and the failure of elevated roads and old bridges."
+
+[144.520–146.160]
+
+"Most buildings would probably be okay,"
+
+[146.340–149.680]
+
+"although this anchored firmly into bedrock might start to behave unpredictably."
+
+[150.040–152.540]
+
+"After a year, gravity would be 5 percent stronger,"
+
+[152.700–155.240]
+
+"and the ground underneath structures would have expanded by 5 percent."
+
+[155.360–157.020]
+
+"You would probably notice the weight gain,"
+
+[157.160–159.220]
+
+"and you would definitely notice the failure of roads,"
+
+[159.500–161.800]
+
+"bridges, power lines, satellites, and undersea cables."
+
+[162.200–164.620]
+
+"Your pendulum clock would now be ahead by five days."
+
+[165.260–167.840]
+
+"After five years, gravity would be 25 percent stronger."
+
+[168.200–170.260]
+
+"If you weighed 70 kilograms in the expansion started,"
+
+[170.260–171.460]
+
+"you'd weigh 88 now."
+
+[171.960–173.620]
+
+"Most of our infrastructure would have collapsed."
+
+[173.940–176.380]
+
+"The cause would be the ground expanding by 25 percent,"
+
+[176.560–177.520]
+
+"not the increased gravity."
+
+[177.960–180.180]
+
+"Surprisingly, most skyscrapers would hold up fine"
+
+[180.180–181.180]
+
+"under much higher gravity."
+
+[181.540–182.620]
+
+"The limiting factor isn't weight,"
+
+[182.860–185.700]
+
+"but sheer force is like wind or the ground expanding."
+
+[186.220–188.800]
+
+"After 10 years, gravity would be 50 percent stronger."
+
+[189.260–190.720]
+
+"We'll assume the atmosphere is expanding too."
+
+[191.000–193.200]
+
+"Otherwise, there wouldn't be enough to cover the growing earth,"
+
+[193.380–195.460]
+
+"and the air would by now be getting too thin to breathe."
+
+[195.940–196.980]
+
+"With an expanding atmosphere,"
+
+[196.980–199.740]
+
+"surface air pressure would rise due to both increased gravity"
+
+[199.740–200.480]
+
+"and more air,"
+
+[200.680–202.360]
+
+"but we'd be okay for a little while longer."
+
+[202.840–205.300]
+
+"After 40 years, Earth's surface gravity would have tripled."
+
+[205.720–207.900]
+
+"At this point, even the strongest humans would be able"
+
+[207.900–209.700]
+
+"to walk only with very great difficulty."
+
+[210.160–211.600]
+
+"Breathing the thick air would be a challenge."
+
+[211.960–212.500]
+
+"Trees would collapse,"
+
+[212.780–214.420]
+
+"and crops wouldn't stand up under their own weight."
+
+[214.940–217.960]
+
+"After 100 years, we'd be experiencing over six G's of gravity."
+
+[218.300–220.660]
+
+"Not only would we be unable to move around to find food,"
+
+[220.940–223.160]
+
+"but our hearts would be unable to pump blood to our brains."
+
+[223.660–226.460]
+
+"Only small insects and sea animals would be physically able"
+
+[226.460–227.120]
+
+"to move around."
+
+[227.600–229.300]
+
+"On top of that, at somewhere around this point,"
+
+[229.480–232.320]
+
+"even ordinary air becomes toxic due to higher oxygen levels."
+
+[232.700–234.900]
+
+"Perhaps humans could survive and control pressure chambers"
+
+[234.900–237.340]
+
+"by keeping our bodies horizontal and tended to by robots,"
+
+[237.620–239.520]
+
+"but this is about as far as we're going to make it."
+
+[240.040–241.720]
+
+"With the Earth eventually become a black hole,"
+
+[242.180–244.740]
+
+"it's hard to answer that because the premise of Dennis' question"
+
+[244.740–248.240]
+
+"is that the radius steadily expands while the density stays the same."
+
+[248.580–251.000]
+
+"Whereas to make a black hole, the density increases."
+
+[251.640–254.320]
+
+"Under realistic physics, by adding more mass to the Earth,"
+
+[254.320–256.740]
+
+"we would eventually exceed the strength of the chemical bonds"
+
+[256.740–258.480]
+
+"to withstand the growing internal stresses,"
+
+[258.760–260.440]
+
+"and the Earth would contract rather than expand,"
+
+[260.860–263.200]
+
+"collapsing into something like a sputtering white dwarf star"
+
+[263.200–265.040]
+
+"held up by electron-generacy pressure."
+
+[265.500–268.060]
+
+"Then, after around 1500 years of expansion,"
+
+[268.440–270.780]
+
+"if the Earth's mass kept increasing according to the original premise,"
+
+[271.160–274.040]
+
+"after 1500 years, the Earth would pass the Chandrashaker limit"
+
+[274.040–276.580]
+
+"for white dwarf stars and become a black hole."
+
+[277.060–278.620]
+
+"But before it gets that far,"
+
+[279.000–281.320]
+
+"it's a shame humans wouldn't survive 300 years"
+
+[281.320–283.380]
+
+"because at this point, something really neat would happen."
+
+[283.380–286.160]
+
+"As the Earth grew, the Moon would, like all our satellites,"
+
+[286.480–287.620]
+
+"gradually spiral inward."
+
+[288.020–291.020]
+
+"After several centuries, it would be close enough to the swollen Earth"
+
+[291.020–293.000]
+
+"that the tidal forces between Earth and the Moon"
+
+[293.000–296.180]
+
+"would be stronger than the gravitational forces holding the Moon together."
+
+[296.600–298.840]
+
+"When the Moon passed this boundary, called the Rochel limit,"
+
+[299.200–300.460]
+
+"it would gradually break apart,"
+
+[300.720–303.780]
+
+"and the Earth would, for a short time, have rings."
+

+#!/usr/bin/env python3
+"""Self-contained validator for what_if_all_visible_light_was_a_single_beam.
+Run: python3 00_source/verify.py   (from this video's project root)
+Stdlib only. Prints PASS or raises AssertionError on the first failure.
+"""
+import csv
+import json
+import re
+from pathlib import Path
+
+ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parent.parent
+
+def read_csv(name):
+    with open(ROOT / "02_analysis" / name, newline="") as f:
+        return list(csv.DictReader(f))
+
+def read_text(rel):
+    return (ROOT / rel).read_text()
+
+# ---- Timeline coverage ----
+timeline = read_csv("TIMELINE.csv")
+assert len(timeline) == 33, f"expected 33 states, got {len(timeline)}"
+rows = sorted(timeline, key=lambda r: int(r["IN"]))
+expected_in = 0
+total_frames = 0
+for r in rows:
+    in_f, out_f = int(r["IN"]), int(r["OUT"])
+    assert in_f == expected_in, f"gap/overlap before state {r['STATE_ID']}: expected IN={expected_in}, got {in_f}"
+    assert out_f >= in_f, f"invalid range in state {r['STATE_ID']}"
+    dur_frames = int(r["DURATION"].split("/")[0])
+    assert dur_frames == out_f - in_f + 1, f"duration mismatch in state {r['STATE_ID']}"
+    expected_in = out_f + 1
+    total_frames += dur_frames
+assert total_frames == 3718, f"total frames {total_frames} != 3718"
+assert rows[-1]["OUT"] == "3717", "timeline does not reach the last frame (3717)"
+
+shots = sorted(set(r["SHOT_ID"] for r in timeline), key=lambda s: int(s[1:]))
+assert shots == [f"S{n:02d}" for n in range(1, 16)], f"unexpected shot set: {shots}"
+
+# ---- Asset manifest ----
+assets = read_csv("ASSET_MANIFEST.csv")
+assert len(assets) == 30, f"expected 30 assets, got {len(assets)}"
+asset_ids = set(a["ASSET_ID"] for a in assets)
+assert len(asset_ids) == 30, "duplicate ASSET_ID found"
+
+def split_ids(s):
+    return [x.strip() for x in s.split(";") if x.strip()]
+
+referenced_assets = set()
+for r in timeline:
+    referenced_assets |= set(split_ids(r["ASSET_IDS"]))
+missing = referenced_assets - asset_ids
+assert not missing, f"TIMELINE references unknown asset IDs: {missing}"
+
+# ---- Motion events ----
+motions = read_csv("MOTION_EVENTS.csv")
+assert len(motions) == 18, f"expected 18 motion events, got {len(motions)}"
+motion_ids = set(m["MOTION_ID"] for m in motions)
+assert motion_ids == {f"A{n:02d}" for n in range(1, 19)}, f"unexpected motion ID set: {sorted(motion_ids)}"
+for m in motions:
+    assert m["SHOT_ID"] in shots, f"motion {m['MOTION_ID']} references unknown shot {m['SHOT_ID']}"
+    assert int(m["OUT"]) >= int(m["IN"]), f"motion {m['MOTION_ID']} has invalid IN/OUT"
+
+# every non-static-hold state's MOTION_IDS field (when not N/A) must resolve
+referenced_motions = set()
+for r in timeline:
+    for mid in split_ids(r["MOTION_IDS"]):
+        if mid.startswith("A") and mid[1:].isdigit():
+            referenced_motions.add(mid)
+missing_m = referenced_motions - motion_ids
+assert not missing_m, f"TIMELINE references unknown motion IDs: {missing_m}"
+
+# ---- CapCut guide ----
+capcut = read_text("03_capcut/CAPCUT_REBUILD.md")
+for s in shots:
+    assert re.search(rf"^## {s} ", capcut, re.M), f"CAPCUT_REBUILD.md missing header for {s}"
+for mid in sorted(motion_ids):
+    assert mid in capcut, f"CAPCUT_REBUILD.md never references motion {mid}"
+
+# ---- Image prompts ----
+img_prompts = read_text("04_image_to_video/IMAGE_PROMPTS.md")
+img_headers = re.findall(r"^## (IMG\d+)$", img_prompts, re.M)
+assert len(img_headers) == 13, f"expected 13 IMG headers, got {len(img_headers)}"
+assert img_headers == [f"IMG{n:02d}" for n in range(1, 14)], f"unexpected/non-sequential IMG headers: {img_headers}"
+assert img_prompts.count("TEXT BAKED: NO") == 12, "expected 12 standalone image prompts declaring TEXT BAKED: NO (IMG08 is a reuse stub with no prompt of its own)"
+
+# ---- Animation prompts ----
+anim = read_text("04_image_to_video/ANIMATION_PROMPTS.md")
+anim_headers = re.findall(r"^## (A\d+)$", anim, re.M)
+assert set(anim_headers) == motion_ids, f"ANIMATION_PROMPTS.md headers {sorted(anim_headers)} != motion set {sorted(motion_ids)}"
+for block in re.split(r"^## A\d+$", anim, flags=re.M)[1:]:
+    m = re.search(r"ANIMATION PROMPT:\s*(.+?)(?:\n##|\Z)", block, re.S)
+    assert m, "a motion block is missing its ANIMATION PROMPT line"
+    prompt_text = m.group(1).strip()
+    assert 1 <= len(prompt_text) <= 500, f"animation prompt out of 1-500 char range ({len(prompt_text)} chars)"
+
+# ---- I2V guide ----
+i2v = read_text("04_image_to_video/I2V_REBUILD.md")
+for s in shots:
+    assert re.search(rf"^## {s} ", i2v, re.M), f"I2V_REBUILD.md missing header for {s}"
+
+# ---- Audio map sanity ----
+audio_map = read_text("05_audio/AUDIO_MAP.md")
+assert "UNAVAILABLE" in audio_map, "AUDIO_MAP.md should record that transcript is unavailable"
+assert audio_map.count("75.226") + audio_map.count("75.2") >= 1, "AUDIO_MAP.md missing first measured silence gap"
+
+# ---- Cross-project markdown link check ----
+link_re = re.compile(r"\[[^\]]*\]\(([^)]+)\)")
+for md_file in ROOT.rglob("*.md"):
+    text = md_file.read_text(errors="ignore")
+    for target in link_re.findall(text):
+        if target.startswith("http") or target.startswith("#"):
+            continue
+        target_path = (md_file.parent / target.split("#")[0]).resolve()
+        assert target_path.exists(), f"{md_file.relative_to(ROOT)} has a broken link to {target}"
+
+# ---- RUN_STATE.json counts (if present and populated) ----
+run_state_path = ROOT / "RUN_STATE.json"
+if run_state_path.exists():
+    run_state = json.loads(run_state_path.read_text())
+    counts = run_state.get("counts")
+    if counts:
+        assert counts["shots"] == 15
+        assert counts["visual_states"] == 33
+        assert counts["unique_assets"] == 30
+        assert counts["motion_events"] == 18
+        assert counts["unique_images"] == 13
+
+print("PASS: timeline coverage, asset/motion ID cross-refs, CapCut shot+motion coverage, "
+      "image/animation prompt counts and length limits, I2V shot coverage, audio map sanity, "
+      "and file links.")

+# Visual DNA — what_if_all_visible_light_was_a_single_beam
+
+Global, repeated production patterns. Scene-specific detail lives in `TIMELINE.csv`; this file is not repeated there.
+
+| Dimension | Repeated rule | Exceptions / limits |
+|---|---|---|
+| CHARACTER DNA | One recurring minimal stick-figure (circle head, thin line limbs, holding a paper) in S01 only; a labeled human silhouette (line-art) in S02 only. No character reappears across shots. | No characters appear after S02; the rest of the video is diagrams/objects only. |
+| ENVIRONMENT DNA | Three backdrop families reused across most shots: (1) plain black starfield (E02, most of the runtime), (2) grey chalkboard (E01, S01 only), (3) side-view cross-section of sky+planetary-arc+continent (E03, S04 and S09). | Dusk graveyard (E04) is unique to S06 and does not recur. |
+| OBJECT DNA | A single Earth/Moon iconography family recurs at three levels of realism: shaded/detailed (G09), plain half-lit sphere (G11), and simplified black outline (G13); the Moon is always a small plain grey circle (G14) until it is damaged (G17, red/cracked). | The chalkboard's tiny Earth icon (G02) is a fourth, simpler style used only in S01/S03; it is not the same asset as G09/G11/G13. |
+| COLOR PALETTE | Two-mode palette: neutral grey/black/white for exposition (S01-S03, S07, S10-S12), with a single accent — glowing white for the light source/beam — throughout. Red/pink is reserved exclusively for damage, danger, or destruction (plasma dome, cracks, "NOT SAFE!", the ring, the comet, the shattered Moon). | S06's graveyard is the only shot with a distinct purple-to-pink dusk sky; S01 is the only shot on an off-white/grey chalkboard rather than black. |
+| LIGHTING | Flat, shadeless illustration lighting throughout; the only "light" rendered as light is the glow/beam graphic itself (G03/G05), used consistently as a bright white radial or linear glow with soft falloff. | None observed. |
+| CAMERA / FRAMING | 9:16 vertical lock. Camera is static (no zoom/dolly/rotation) in 14 of 15 shots. | S06 (graveyard) is the only shot with OBSERVED camera motion: a lateral pan across a row of gravestones. Do not add camera motion to any other shot. |
+| COMPOSITION | Recurring "vertical beam down the center third" composition anchors S01, S04, S05, S07, S08, S09, S11, S12, S13 — the beam or its target sits on/near the vertical centerline with labels/arrows branching to the sides. | S02, S03, S06, S10, S14, S15 break from this (S02/S03 have no discrete target object yet; S06/S14/S15 have no beam in frame). |
+| TYPOGRAPHY | Two caption styles: a thin hand-drawn-style sans caption for callouts/labels/stats (T01, T03, T04, T05, T07), and a bolder carved/serif-ish style reserved for the tombstone text (T06). | Exact typeface is UNKNOWN/unverifiable; recreate by visual matching only, per fidelity rules. |
+| GRAPHICS | Arrow-and-label callout pairs (thin line arrow + short caption) are the dominant graphic device, appearing in S01, S04, S05, S07, S11. | The subatomic-particle glyphs (G04) and the twin ring effects (G12 twilight-ring vs. G15 shockwave-ring) are one-off/twice-only devices — do not conflate the two rings, they differ in scale, speed, and narrative meaning. |
+| ILLUSTRATION / 3D STYLE | Flat 2D vector-style illustration throughout; no 3D rendering, no photographic elements, no particle-simulation-grade detail (sparks/debris are simple flecks and jagged line strokes, not simulated). | None observed. |
+| DEPTH | Consistently shallow/flat: foreground subject + plain background, no midground layer, in every shot. | None observed. |
+| MOTION LANGUAGE | Motion is almost entirely "reveal" (fade-in of text/graphics) or "radial growth" (dome, rings, starburst) rather than translation of a whole camera or a whole rigid object across the frame. The two exceptions — the S06 pan and the S12→S13 Moon flight — are the only translation-type motions in the video. | Per the reference-fidelity rule, no zoom, parallax, particle system, or camera shake should be added anywhere motion is not explicitly listed in `MOTION_EVENTS.csv`. |

+## Evidence and measurement conventions

+"The intense light from the destruction would itself, however, illuminate the moon, and this reflected moonlight alone could be enough to burn you to death, just in time for the incendiary twilight to wrap around the planet, bringing on quantum-final sunrise."
+
+[106.580–113.900] S00020
+
+"But Earth may not be entirely doomed. The Earth can only spend a maximum of about seven minutes in the path of the beam before our orbit carries us out of the way."
+
+[114.300–122.420] S00021
+
+"Everyone on the surface would still be cooked, of course, and much of the atmosphere in exterior would be lost, but the bulk of the Earth would probably remain as a testament to humanity's horrible ideas."
+

+what_if_all_visible_light_was_a_single_beam,S00001,0.000,5.980,What if all the suns output of visible light were bundled up into a laser-like beam that had a diameter of around one meter once it reached the Earth?,W00001,W00030,30,,
+what_if_all_visible_light_was_a_single_beam,S00002,6.520,9.440,"If you were standing in the path of the beam, you would obviously die pretty quickly.",W00031,W00046,16,,
+what_if_all_visible_light_was_a_single_beam,S00003,9.820,14.360,You wouldn't really die of anything in the traditional sense? You would just stop being biology and start being physics.,W00047,W00066,20,,
+what_if_all_visible_light_was_a_single_beam,S00004,14.940,20.420,The Earth receives about 0.004% as much energy from the sun in an entire day as the sun emits every second.,W00067,W00089,23,,

+what_if_all_visible_light_was_a_single_beam,S00007,33.840,39.260,"The radiation would vaporize everything in sight and start stripping away the Earth's surface, like a hydrogen bomb, only much more violent.",W00154,W00175,22,,
+what_if_all_visible_light_was_a_single_beam,S00008,39.680,44.320,"But the Earth is big enough to protect people on the other side, at least for a bit, from the direct effects of the sun beam.",W00176,W00201,26,,
+what_if_all_visible_light_was_a_single_beam,S00009,44.680,47.560,"They're still not going to make it, but what exactly would they die from?",W00202,W00215,14,,
+what_if_all_visible_light_was_a_single_beam,S00010,48.240,51.320,"Turns out, twilight, or moonlight, it depends on the details.",W00216,W00225,10,,
+what_if_all_visible_light_was_a_single_beam,S00011,51.940,55.820,Twilight is light from the out-of-sight sun that reaches you by scattering off the atmosphere.,W00226,W00242,17,,
+what_if_all_visible_light_was_a_single_beam,S00012,56.160,61.160,"When the beam of light hit the Earth, everything from infrared radiation to x-rays would flood into the atmosphere, turning into plasma.",W00243,W00265,23,,
+what_if_all_visible_light_was_a_single_beam,S00013,61.680,69.560,"Plasma is relatively transparent to x-rays, so those would pass through and dump their energy into the non-plasma air around it, heating it enough to give off its own substantial thermal radiation.",W00266,W00299,34,,
+what_if_all_visible_light_was_a_single_beam,S00014,69.940,74.940,"In general, a lot of this radiation would escape into space, where we don't need to worry about it unless it gets reflected back to Earth.",W00300,W00325,26,,
+what_if_all_visible_light_was_a_single_beam,S00015,75.400,78.040,"Unfortunately, a portion of the radiation would stay within the atmosphere.",W00326,W00336,11,,
+what_if_all_visible_light_was_a_single_beam,S00016,78.040,83.160,"A bubble of heat and light would wrap around the Earth, a twilight inferno, rapidly heating the atmosphere in surface as it went.",W00337,W00359,23,,
+what_if_all_visible_light_was_a_single_beam,S00017,83.580,90.340,"What's more, much of the matter around the sun beam's contact point would be blasted into space, where it would reflect infrared light back down beyond the horizon.",W00360,W00387,28,,

+"""Self-contained validator for what_if_earths_water_suddenly_disappear.
+Run: python3 00_source/verify.py   (from this video's project root)
+Stdlib only. Prints PASS or raises AssertionError on the first failure.
+"""
+import csv
+import json
+import re
+from pathlib import Path
+
+ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parent.parent
+
+def read_csv(name):
+    with open(ROOT / "02_analysis" / name, newline="") as f:
+        return list(csv.DictReader(f))
+
+def read_text(rel):
+    return (ROOT / rel).read_text()
+
+# ---- Timeline coverage ----
+timeline = read_csv("TIMELINE.csv")
+assert len(timeline) == 47, f"expected 47 states, got {len(timeline)}"
+rows = sorted(timeline, key=lambda r: int(r["IN"]))
+expected_in = 0
+total_frames = 0
+for r in rows:
+    in_f, out_f = int(r["IN"]), int(r["OUT"])
+    assert in_f == expected_in, f"gap/overlap before state {r['STATE_ID']}: expected IN={expected_in}, got {in_f}"
+    assert out_f >= in_f, f"invalid range in state {r['STATE_ID']}"
+    dur_frames = int(r["DURATION"].split("/")[0])
+    assert dur_frames == out_f - in_f + 1, f"duration mismatch in state {r['STATE_ID']}"
+    expected_in = out_f + 1
+    total_frames += dur_frames
+assert total_frames == 4411, f"total frames {total_frames} != 4411"
+assert rows[-1]["OUT"] == "4410", "timeline does not reach the last frame (4410)"
+
+shots = sorted(set(r["SHOT_ID"] for r in timeline), key=lambda s: int(s[1:]))
+assert shots == [f"S{n:02d}" for n in range(1, 19)], f"unexpected shot set: {shots}"
+
+# ---- Asset manifest ----
+assets = read_csv("ASSET_MANIFEST.csv")
+assert len(assets) == 41, f"expected 41 assets, got {len(assets)}"
+asset_ids = set(a["ASSET_ID"] for a in assets)
+assert len(asset_ids) == 41, "duplicate ASSET_ID found"
+
+def split_ids(s):
+    return [x.strip() for x in s.split(";") if x.strip()]
+
+referenced_assets = set()
+for r in timeline:
+    referenced_assets |= set(split_ids(r["ASSET_IDS"]))
+missing = referenced_assets - asset_ids
+assert not missing, f"TIMELINE references unknown asset IDs: {missing}"
+unused = asset_ids - referenced_assets
+assert unused <= {"AU01"}, f"unexpected unused assets (only AU01 should be timeline-unreferenced): {unused}"
+
+# ---- Motion events ----
+motions = read_csv("MOTION_EVENTS.csv")
+assert len(motions) == 29, f"expected 29 motion events, got {len(motions)}"
+motion_ids = set(m["MOTION_ID"] for m in motions)
+assert motion_ids == {f"A{n:02d}" for n in range(1, 30)}, f"unexpected motion ID set: {sorted(motion_ids)}"
+for m in motions:
+    assert m["SHOT_ID"] in shots, f"motion {m['MOTION_ID']} references unknown shot {m['SHOT_ID']}"
+    assert int(m["OUT"]) >= int(m["IN"]), f"motion {m['MOTION_ID']} has invalid IN/OUT"
+
+referenced_motions = set()
+for r in timeline:
+    for mid in split_ids(r["MOTION_IDS"]):
+        if mid.startswith("A") and mid[1:].isdigit():
+            referenced_motions.add(mid)
+missing_m = referenced_motions - motion_ids
+assert not missing_m, f"TIMELINE references unknown motion IDs: {missing_m}"
+assert referenced_motions == motion_ids, f"not every motion is referenced from TIMELINE: unreferenced={motion_ids - referenced_motions}"

+
+# ---- Image prompts ----
+img_prompts = read_text("04_image_to_video/IMAGE_PROMPTS.md")
+img_headers = re.findall(r"^## (IMG\d+)$", img_prompts, re.M)
+assert len(img_headers) == 24, f"expected 24 IMG headers, got {len(img_headers)}"
+assert img_headers == [f"IMG{n:02d}" for n in range(1, 25)], f"unexpected/non-sequential IMG headers: {img_headers}"
+baked_yes = len(re.findall(r"^TEXT BAKED: YES", img_prompts, re.M))
+baked_no = len(re.findall(r"^TEXT BAKED: NO", img_prompts, re.M))
+assert baked_yes == 4, f"expected exactly 4 TEXT BAKED: YES, got {baked_yes}"
+assert baked_no == 20, f"expected exactly 20 TEXT BAKED: NO, got {baked_no}"
+
+# ---- Animation prompts ----
+anim = read_text("04_image_to_video/ANIMATION_PROMPTS.md")
+anim_headers = re.findall(r"^## (A\d+)$", anim, re.M)
+assert set(anim_headers) == motion_ids, f"ANIMATION_PROMPTS.md headers {sorted(anim_headers)} != motion set {sorted(motion_ids)}"
+for block in re.split(r"^## A\d+$", anim, flags=re.M)[1:]:
+    m = re.search(r"ANIMATION PROMPT:\s*(.+?)(?:\n##|\Z)", block, re.S)
+    assert m, "a motion block is missing its ANIMATION PROMPT line"
+    prompt_text = m.group(1).strip()

+# ---- I2V guide ----
+i2v = read_text("04_image_to_video/I2V_REBUILD.md")
+for s in shots:

+
+# ---- Cross-project markdown link check ----
+link_re = re.compile(r"\[[^\]]*\]\(([^)]+)\)")
+for md_file in ROOT.rglob("*.md"):
+    text = md_file.read_text(errors="ignore")
+    for target in link_re.findall(text):

+# Visual DNA — what_if_earths_water_suddenly_disappear
+
+Global, evidence-supported production characteristics. Scene-specific detail lives in `TIMELINE.csv`; this file states only what recurs across the whole video.
+
+## CHARACTER DNA
+All human figures are minimal black-outline stick figures (circle head, single-line limbs, no facial features beyond occasional simple marks) — the recognizable "xkcd what if?" house style, consistent with the illustration family used elsewhere in this project. The host (C01) is the only character who recurs across non-adjacent shots (S01, S13, S15); every other character is scene-local.
+
+## ENVIRONMENT DNA
+Nine distinct backdrop environments (E01–E09), each confined to its own shot(s), reflecting a genuinely multi-scene explainer rather than a single locked set. All backgrounds are flat line-art with sparse color fill (white/gray/black, plus red used only for warning/danger/branding moments — title card, credits, heat gradient, engulfment rays).
+
+## OBJECT DNA
+Small watercraft (sailboat/kayak) and ship/fleet icon marks recur at multiple scales across the beach and depth-scale shots (O02, O05) — the same simple silhouette redrawn larger or smaller depending on the diagram's zoom level. Creature silhouettes (fish/whale/dolphin, O07) are the only object explicitly reused across non-adjacent shots (the S10 jar-diagram sequence and the S16/S17 aquarium epilogue), functioning as a visual callback.
+
+## COLOR PALETTE
+Overwhelmingly black-line-on-white/gray, matching this project's other xkcd-style sources. Red is reserved for exactly four purposes: the title card (S02), the runaway-heat gradient (S14), the sun-engulfment rays (S15), and the credits card (S18) — i.e., red consistently marks "branding" or "danger/heat" moments, never ordinary narrative content.
+
+## LIGHTING
+Flat, shadowless line-art throughout; no lighting model beyond solid-fill vs. outline. The only "lighting" event is the red gradient wash in S14/S15, which is a color/heat metaphor rather than a literal light source change.
+
+## CAMERA / FRAMING
+No physical camera; all "shots" are discrete diagram compositions cut against each other. Every shot uses a single locked framing internally (no pans, no handheld motion) — the only zoom-like event is the S09 zoom-out from the dual-panel depth comparison to the full Mariana Trench profile (A14), which is a diagram-scale transform, not a camera move. 17 of 18 shot boundaries are corroborated by measured `ffmpeg scdet` score spikes (see `00_source/SOURCE_MANIFEST.md`); the 18th is simply the video's natural end.
+
+## COMPOSITION
+Two recurring composition templates: (1) the "host" template — a stick figure beside a blackboard occupying the left third of frame, content drawn inside the blackboard on the right two-thirds (S01, S13, S15); (2) the "cross-section" template — a horizontal reference line (sea level or ground level) with a labeled vertical/depth scale, used for every water-level and geological diagram (S04–S09, S14).
+
+## TYPOGRAPHY
+Three recurring text systems (T01–T03, see `ASSET_MANIFEST.csv`): a bold Q-card/question style, a bold aside/exclamation caption style (VACUUM, GASP!, WHEEZE!, WORSE? FOR WHO?, Hi!), and a small measurement/chemistry label style (depth numbers, timer values, chemical formulas). All appear to be a single consistent sans-serif family at different weights/sizes rather than distinct fonts.
+
+## GRAPHICS
+14 distinct overlay graphics (G01–G14), the largest graphic inventory in this project to date, reflecting the video's greater topical range (drainage physics, marine biology, atmospheric chemistry, geology, astronomy). The "measurement overlay system" (G04: timers, scale bars, depth axes, brackets) is the single most-reused graphic, spanning 6 shots (S05–S10).
+
+## ILLUSTRATION / 3D STYLE
+Pure 2D hand-drawn-style vector line art; no 3D, no photographic elements, no camera-realistic lighting or texture anywhere in the video.
+
+## DEPTH
+No true depth-of-field or parallax; apparent "depth" in the cross-section diagrams (S04–S09) is communicated entirely through a vertical depth-scale axis and relative object size, not through actual foreground/background blur or layering.
+
+## MOTION LANGUAGE
+Motion in this video is dominated by STATE_REPLACEMENT (content swaps: graphics appearing/clearing, fills changing) and SEQUENTIAL continuous changes (fire spreading, gradient intensifying, objects descending) — see `MOTION_EVENTS.csv`. Only two motion events are genuine physical translations of a character/object through space (A03 sailboat capsize, A20 figure+dog+boat departure); everything else is either a value/label change, a fill/color change, or a fade.
+
+## TRANSITION LANGUAGE
+Nearly all 18 shot boundaries are hard CUTs. Two exceptions are evidenced by measured near-silence audio gaps and gray full-frame intermediate frames: the S06→S07 boundary (fades to solid gray before the deep-ocean panel appears, corroborated by a measured 58.7–58.9s audio near-silence gap) and the S07 shot's own opening (also preceded by the same fade). No wipes, slides, or other transition types were observed.
+
+## ASSET REUSE PATTERN
+Lower overall reuse than `weird_and_worrying_questions` in absolute terms (most graphics/objects/environments are single-shot, reflecting the wide topical range) but higher character/text-system reuse for the recurring "host" device, which structurally bookends and punctuates the video (S01 intro question → S13 mid-video punchline → S15 closing epilogue). The measurement-overlay system (G04) and the underwater cross-section backdrop (E04) are the two most-reused non-character assets (6 and 6 shots respectively... actually E04 spans 4 shots, G04 spans 6 — see `ASSET_MANIFEST.csv` for exact OTHER_APPEARANCES counts).

+[00.000–01.900]
+
+"This question comes from Joanna, who asks,"
+
+[02.180–04.620]
+
+"what would happen if all the bodies of water on Earth magically disappeared?"
+
+[05.200–08.020]
+
+"As is often the case with these questions, everyone would die."
+
+[10.000–13.420]
+
+"The first people to notice would be swimmers and boaters for obvious reasons."
+
+[13.820–17.340]
+
+"To avoid a glass-fifty scenario, we're going to assume all the waters are placed by air,"
+
+[17.540–19.960]
+
+"and we'll assume that by all bodies of water disappeared,"
+
+[20.120–23.480]
+
+"Joanna's including underground bodies like aquafers, waterfers and ice caps,"
+
+[23.780–26.160]
+
+"and artificial bodies of water like swimming pools and water tanks."
+
+[26.740–28.780]
+
+"Most people swim in water, which is relatively shallow,"
+
+[28.780–30.720]
+
+"so most of them would survive the fall to the bottom,"
+
+[30.760–32.080]
+
+"albeit with a few broken bones."
+
+[32.780–36.400]
+
+"Within the first second, a large fraction of the boats in lakes, rivers and shallow harbors"
+
+[36.400–39.180]
+
+"would also crash to the bottom, and many of those on board would survive."
+
+[39.720–41.520]
+
+"Boats out in the ocean would take longer to fall."
+
+[41.880–45.140]
+
+"Over the next five seconds, a wave of crashes would spread outward from the continents,"
+
+[45.280–47.860]
+
+"as boats struck the continental shelf farther and farther from shore."
+
+[48.300–49.820]
+
+"These falls would leave no survivors."
+
+[50.460–54.300]
+
+"After the first six or seven seconds, there would be a brief low in the ship destruction rate."
+
+[54.300–57.540]
+
+"Condon and L-shelves drop off steeply, and most of the ships out over the deep sea"
+
+[57.540–58.440]
+
+"would take longer to fall."
+
+[58.840–60.860]
+
+"The Titanic sank in about two miles of water,"
+
+[60.960–64.220]
+
+"with two halves of the ship taking between five and fifteen minutes to reach the bottom."
+
+[64.520–67.200]
+
+"Without the ocean there, it would have reached the bottom at about 30 seconds,"
+
+[67.460–68.840]
+
+"striking at airliner cruising speed."
+
+[69.280–72.160]
+
+"Within the first minute, just about every large ship would be on the bottom."
+
+[72.580–75.600]
+
+"The final boat would probably be a small sailboat or life raft that happened"
+
+[75.600–77.960]
+
+"to be crossing a deep ocean trench when the water vanished."
+
+[78.400–80.340]
+
+"If there were a sea plane floating out on the deep ocean,"
+
+[80.480–83.840]
+
+"it could conceivably survive, although it would take some luck and quick thinking by the pilot."
+
+[83.840–87.800]
+
+"The plane would initially drop, but as it gained speed, it would tend to pull out into a glide,"
+
+[87.980–91.680]
+
+"and the pilot would have a bit of time to try to start the engine or land on the sea floor like the glider."
+
+[92.200–95.680]
+
+"Fish, whales, dolphins, and nearly all marine life would also die out in the first few minutes."
+
+[96.100–99.060]
+
+"Even if they survived the fall, anything that breathes oxygen dissolved in water"
+
+[99.060–101.660]
+
+"like fish would quickly suffocate on the now dry ocean floor."
+
+[102.040–105.540]
+
+"An air breathing animal would likely suffer the same slow suffocation and dehydration"
+
+[105.540–106.920]
+
+"that regularly kills beached whales."
+
+[107.440–109.460]
+
+"But then the really weird stuff starts."
+
+[110.000–113.300]
+
+"Without pools of water to drink from, people and most animals would dehydrate and die"
+
+[113.300–114.080]
+
+"in a matter of days."
+
+[114.460–117.680]
+
+"Without evaporation from lakes and oceans beating the water cycle, it would stop raining."
+
+[118.020–120.700]
+
+"And within a few weeks, plants would start weathering in the ever-dryer air."
+
+[121.140–123.500]
+
+"Within months, mass forest dyes would be in."
+
+[124.040–127.080]
+
+"Huge amounts of dry, dead vegetation lead inevitably to fire,"
+
+[127.420–129.640]
+
+"and within a few years, most of the world's forests would burn."
+
+[130.180–134.440]
+
+"Forests store huge amounts of carpet dioxide, and this burning would roughly double the amount of greenhouse gas"
+
+[134.440–136.300]
+
+"in the atmosphere, accelerating global warming."
+
+[136.880–140.860]
+
+"All in all, Joanna's scenario would result in virtually all life dying out pretty fast,"
+
+[140.860–143.020]
+
+"but then things get even worse."
+
+[143.720–149.140]
+
+"Without a water cycle to weather rocks, the carbon silicate feedback system which acts to stabilize Earth's climate would shut down."
+
+[149.500–152.060]
+
+"Without this feedback, volcanic CO2 would build up in our atmosphere,"
+
+[152.220–154.580]
+
+"eventually leading to scorching temperatures similar to Venus."
+
+[155.200–157.240]
+
+"We are eventually going to lose our oceans anyway."
+
+[157.600–160.860]
+
+"As the sun gets older and hotter, water will eventually start escaping through evaporation"
+
+[161.380–163.320]
+
+"and the planet will dry out and heat up."
+
+[163.640–166.740]
+
+"However, the loss of the oceans doesn't seem like something worth worrying much about,"
+
+[166.920–169.700]
+
+"since the oceans are going to be here long after our species is gone."
+
+[169.700–172.120]
+
+"Unless Joanna ruins everything."
+

+#!/usr/bin/env python3
+"""Self-contained validator for what_if_the_moon_were_made_of_protons.
+Run: python3 00_source/verify.py   (from this video's project root)
+Stdlib only. Prints PASS or raises AssertionError on the first failure.
+"""
+import csv
+import json
+import re
+from pathlib import Path
+
+ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parent.parent
+
+def read_csv(name):
+    with open(ROOT / "02_analysis" / name, newline="") as f:
+        return list(csv.DictReader(f))
+
+def read_text(rel):
+    return (ROOT / rel).read_text()
+
+# ---- Timeline coverage ----
+timeline = read_csv("TIMELINE.csv")
+assert len(timeline) == 32, f"expected 32 states, got {len(timeline)}"
+rows = sorted(timeline, key=lambda r: int(r["IN"]))
+expected_in = 0
+total_frames = 0
+for r in rows:
+    in_f, out_f = int(r["IN"]), int(r["OUT"])
+    assert in_f == expected_in, f"gap/overlap before state {r['STATE_ID']}: expected IN={expected_in}, got {in_f}"
+    assert out_f >= in_f, f"invalid range in state {r['STATE_ID']}"
+    dur_frames = int(r["DURATION"].split("/")[0])
+    assert dur_frames == out_f - in_f + 1, f"duration mismatch in state {r['STATE_ID']}"
+    expected_in = out_f + 1
+    total_frames += dur_frames
+assert total_frames == 2114, f"total frames {total_frames} != 2114"
+assert rows[-1]["OUT"] == "2113", "timeline does not reach the last frame (2113)"
+
+shots = sorted(set(r["SHOT_ID"] for r in timeline), key=lambda s: int(s[1:]))
+assert shots == [f"S{n:02d}" for n in range(1, 10)], f"unexpected shot set: {shots}"
+
+# ---- Asset manifest ----
+assets = read_csv("ASSET_MANIFEST.csv")
+assert len(assets) == 27, f"expected 27 assets, got {len(assets)}"
+asset_ids = set(a["ASSET_ID"] for a in assets)
+assert len(asset_ids) == 27, "duplicate ASSET_ID found"
+
+def split_ids(s):
+    return [x.strip() for x in s.split(";") if x.strip()]
+
+referenced_assets = set()
+for r in timeline:
+    referenced_assets |= set(split_ids(r["ASSET_IDS"]))
+missing = referenced_assets - asset_ids
+assert not missing, f"TIMELINE references unknown asset IDs: {missing}"
+
+# ---- Motion events ----
+motions = read_csv("MOTION_EVENTS.csv")
+assert len(motions) == 24, f"expected 24 motion events, got {len(motions)}"
+motion_ids = set(m["MOTION_ID"] for m in motions)
+assert motion_ids == {f"A{n:02d}" for n in range(1, 25)}, f"unexpected motion ID set: {sorted(motion_ids)}"
+for m in motions:
+    assert m["SHOT_ID"] in shots, f"motion {m['MOTION_ID']} references unknown shot {m['SHOT_ID']}"
+    assert int(m["OUT"]) >= int(m["IN"]), f"motion {m['MOTION_ID']} has invalid IN/OUT"
+
+referenced_motions = set()
+for r in timeline:
+    for mid in split_ids(r["MOTION_IDS"]):
+        if mid.startswith("A") and mid[1:].isdigit():
+            referenced_motions.add(mid)
+missing_m = referenced_motions - motion_ids
+assert not missing_m, f"TIMELINE references unknown motion IDs: {missing_m}"
+
+# ---- CapCut guide ----
+capcut = read_text("03_capcut/CAPCUT_REBUILD.md")
+for s in shots:
+    assert re.search(rf"^## {s} ", capcut, re.M), f"CAPCUT_REBUILD.md missing header for {s}"
+for mid in sorted(motion_ids):
+    assert mid in capcut, f"CAPCUT_REBUILD.md never references motion {mid}"
+
+# ---- Image prompts ----
+img_prompts = read_text("04_image_to_video/IMAGE_PROMPTS.md")
+img_headers = re.findall(r"^## (IMG\d+)$", img_prompts, re.M)
+assert len(img_headers) == 15, f"expected 15 IMG headers, got {len(img_headers)}"
+assert img_headers == [f"IMG{n:02d}" for n in range(1, 16)], f"unexpected/non-sequential IMG headers: {img_headers}"
+assert img_prompts.count("TEXT BAKED: NO") == 15, "expected 15 standalone image prompts declaring TEXT BAKED: NO (no reuse stubs in this video)"
+
+# ---- Animation prompts ----
+anim = read_text("04_image_to_video/ANIMATION_PROMPTS.md")
+anim_headers = re.findall(r"^## (A\d+)$", anim, re.M)
+assert set(anim_headers) == motion_ids, f"ANIMATION_PROMPTS.md headers {sorted(anim_headers)} != motion set {sorted(motion_ids)}"
+for block in re.split(r"^## A\d+$", anim, flags=re.M)[1:]:
+    m = re.search(r"ANIMATION PROMPT:\s*(.+?)(?:\n##|\Z)", block, re.S)
+    assert m, "a motion block is missing its ANIMATION PROMPT line"
+    prompt_text = m.group(1).strip()
+    assert 1 <= len(prompt_text) <= 500, f"animation prompt out of 1-500 char range ({len(prompt_text)} chars)"
+
+# ---- I2V guide ----
+i2v = read_text("04_image_to_video/I2V_REBUILD.md")
+for s in shots:
+    assert re.search(rf"^## {s} ", i2v, re.M), f"I2V_REBUILD.md missing header for {s}"
+
+# ---- Audio map sanity ----
+audio_map = read_text("05_audio/AUDIO_MAP.md")
+assert "UNAVAILABLE" in audio_map, "AUDIO_MAP.md should record that transcript is unavailable"
+assert "26.083" in audio_map, "AUDIO_MAP.md missing a measured silence gap"
+
+# ---- Cross-project markdown link check ----
+link_re = re.compile(r"\[[^\]]*\]\(([^)]+)\)")
+for md_file in ROOT.rglob("*.md"):
+    text = md_file.read_text(errors="ignore")
+    for target in link_re.findall(text):
+        if target.startswith("http") or target.startswith("#"):
+            continue
+        target_path = (md_file.parent / target.split("#")[0]).resolve()
+        assert target_path.exists(), f"{md_file.relative_to(ROOT)} has a broken link to {target}"
+
+# ---- RUN_STATE.json counts (if present and populated) ----
+run_state_path = ROOT / "RUN_STATE.json"
+if run_state_path.exists():
+    run_state = json.loads(run_state_path.read_text())
+    counts = run_state.get("counts")
+    if counts:
+        assert counts["shots"] == 9
+        assert counts["visual_states"] == 32
+        assert counts["unique_assets"] == 27
+        assert counts["motion_events"] == 24
+        assert counts["unique_images"] == 15
+
+print("PASS: timeline coverage, asset/motion ID cross-refs, CapCut shot+motion coverage, "
+      "image/animation prompt counts and length limits, I2V shot coverage, audio map sanity, "
+      "and file links.")

+# Visual DNA — what_if_the_moon_were_made_of_protons
+
+Global, evidence-supported production patterns. Scene-specific detail lives in `TIMELINE.csv`; this file records only what repeats across shots. IDs reference `ASSET_MANIFEST.csv` / `MOTION_EVENTS.csv`.
+
+## CHARACTER DNA
+- Repeated rule: a single plain white-outline stick figure (C01) — round bald head, no facial features beyond simple eyes/mouth marks, thin limb lines — represents the narrator/reactor throughout the diagram-heavy first two-thirds of the video (S01, S02, S04).
+- Exceptions or limits: a second, visually distinct stick figure (C02, wavy/curly hair) appears once, only in S08, for a single joke aside. No other characters appear.
+
+## ENVIRONMENT DNA
+- Repeated rule: two background families alternate — (a) a flat white "whiteboard" canvas (E01) for scientific-diagram shots, and (b) a black background (E03 explosion / E05 starfield) for the more dramatic/cosmic beats. A third, one-off grey palette (E04) marks the single "real-world consequence" cutaway (S07).
+- Exceptions or limits: E02 (ground/horizon line) appears only once, layered onto E01 for S04.
+
+## OBJECT / GRAPHIC DNA
+- Repeated rule: every concept is illustrated with a self-contained hand-drawn-style vector icon (circles, dashed orbit rings, arrows, funnels) labeled with small black text; icons are rarely reused verbatim but repeat a consistent "circle + label" visual grammar (G02/G03/G08/G11 all use a circle-plus-caption pattern; G05/G12/G16 all use an arrow-or-funnel-plus-label pattern).
+- Exceptions or limits: G08 ("ELECTRON MOON") is the only icon drawn twice at different scales (full-size in S05, miniature in S06) — a deliberate callback rather than a new design.
+
+## COLOR PALETTE
+- Repeated rule: near-monochrome black/white/grey linework throughout, with a single reserved accent color — red — used exclusively for two purposes: (1) rejection/annotation marks (G04) and (2) all "aside" caption text (T01: "200,000 MOLES OF MOLES", "DARK ENERGY", "WHAT A BEAUTIFUL DAY", "HO HUM", "LA LA LA").
+- Exceptions or limits: none observed; red never appears on any core diagram label (T03) or dialogue caption (T02).
+
+## LIGHTING
+- Not applicable in the photographic sense — all content is flat vector/sketch illustration. "Lighting" is simulated only via background value: bright/white diagram shots vs. a bright radial flash (S02) vs. solid black (S08/S09).
+
+## CAMERA / FRAMING
+- Repeated rule: every shot uses a static, locked camera — no pans, zooms, or parallax were observed anywhere in the video. All apparent scale change is achieved by redrawing/regenerating graphic elements at a new size (e.g., the growing cloud in S04, the growing circle in S09), never by moving a virtual camera.
+- Exceptions or limits: none. This holds for all 9 shots without exception.

+import csv
+import json
+import re
+from pathlib import Path
+
+ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parent.parent
+
+def read_csv(name):
+    with open(ROOT / "02_analysis" / name, newline="") as f:
+        return list(csv.DictReader(f))
+
+def read_text(rel):
+    return (ROOT / rel).read_text()
+
+# ---- Timeline coverage ----
+timeline = read_csv("TIMELINE.csv")
+assert len(timeline) == 47, f"expected 47 states, got {len(timeline)}"
+rows = sorted(timeline, key=lambda r: int(r["IN"]))
+expected_in = 0
+total_frames = 0
+for r in rows:
+    in_f, out_f = int(r["IN"]), int(r["OUT"])
+    assert in_f == expected_in, f"gap/overlap before state {r['STATE_ID']}: expected IN={expected_in}, got {in_f}"
+    assert out_f >= in_f, f"invalid range in state {r['STATE_ID']}"
+    dur_frames = int(r["DURATION"].split("/")[0])
+    assert dur_frames == out_f - in_f + 1, f"duration mismatch in state {r['STATE_ID']}"
+    expected_in = out_f + 1
+    total_frames += dur_frames
+assert total_frames == 4447, f"total frames {total_frames} != 4447"
+assert rows[-1]["OUT"] == "4446", "timeline does not reach the last frame (4446)"
+
+shots = sorted(set(r["SHOT_ID"] for r in timeline), key=lambda s: int(s[1:]))
+assert shots == [f"S{n:02d}" for n in range(1, 17)], f"unexpected shot set: {shots}"
+
+# ---- Asset manifest ----
+assets = read_csv("ASSET_MANIFEST.csv")
+assert len(assets) == 39, f"expected 39 assets, got {len(assets)}"
+asset_ids = set(a["ASSET_ID"] for a in assets)
+assert len(asset_ids) == 39, "duplicate ASSET_ID found"
+
+def split_ids(s):
+    return [x.strip() for x in s.split(";") if x.strip()]
+
+referenced_assets = set()
+for r in timeline:
+    referenced_assets |= set(split_ids(r["ASSET_IDS"]))
+missing = referenced_assets - asset_ids
+assert not missing, f"TIMELINE references unknown asset IDs: {missing}"
+unused = asset_ids - referenced_assets
+assert unused <= {"AU01"}, f"unexpected unused assets (only AU01 should be timeline-unreferenced): {unused}"
+
+# ---- Motion events ----
+motions = read_csv("MOTION_EVENTS.csv")
+assert len(motions) == 33, f"expected 33 motion events, got {len(motions)}"
+motion_ids = set(m["MOTION_ID"] for m in motions)
+assert motion_ids == {f"A{n:02d}" for n in range(1, 34)}, f"unexpected motion ID set: {sorted(motion_ids)}"
+for m in motions:
+    assert m["SHOT_ID"] in shots, f"motion {m['MOTION_ID']} references unknown shot {m['SHOT_ID']}"
+    assert int(m["OUT"]) >= int(m["IN"]), f"motion {m['MOTION_ID']} has invalid IN/OUT"
+

+for r in timeline:
+    for mid in split_ids(r["MOTION_IDS"]):

+assert referenced_motions == motion_ids, f"not every motion is referenced from TIMELINE: unreferenced={motion_ids - referenced_motions}"

+    assert m, "a motion block is missing its ANIMATION PROMPT line"
+    prompt_text = m.group(1).strip()
+    assert 1 <= len(prompt_text) <= 500, f"animation prompt out of 1-500 char range ({len(prompt_text)} chars)"
+
+# ---- I2V guide ----
+i2v = read_text("04_image_to_video/I2V_REBUILD.md")
+for s in shots:
+    assert re.search(rf"^## {s} ", i2v, re.M), f"I2V_REBUILD.md missing header for {s}"
+
+# ---- Audio map sanity ----
+audio_map = read_text("05_audio/AUDIO_MAP.md")
+assert "UNAVAILABLE" in audio_map, "AUDIO_MAP.md should record that transcript is unavailable"
+assert "18.727" in audio_map, "AUDIO_MAP.md missing a measured silence gap"
+
+# ---- Cross-project markdown link check ----
+link_re = re.compile(r"\[[^\]]*\]\(([^)]+)\)")
+for md_file in ROOT.rglob("*.md"):
+    text = md_file.read_text(errors="ignore")
+    for target in link_re.findall(text):
+        if target.startswith("http") or target.startswith("#"):
+            continue
+        target_path = (md_file.parent / target.split("#")[0]).resolve()
+        assert target_path.exists(), f"{md_file.relative_to(ROOT)} has a broken link to {target}"
+
+# ---- RUN_STATE.json counts (if present and populated) ----
+run_state_path = ROOT / "RUN_STATE.json"
+if run_state_path.exists():
+    run_state = json.loads(run_state_path.read_text())
+    counts = run_state.get("counts")
+    if counts:
+        assert counts["shots"] == 16
+        assert counts["visual_states"] == 47
+        assert counts["unique_assets"] == 39
+        assert counts["motion_events"] == 33
+        assert counts["unique_images"] == 29
+
+print("PASS: timeline coverage, asset/motion ID cross-refs, CapCut shot coverage, "
+      "image/animation prompt counts and length limits, I2V shot coverage, audio map sanity, "
+      "and file links.")

+# Visual DNA — what_would_a_magnitude_15_earthquake_be
+
+Global, evidence-supported production characteristics. Scene-specific detail lives in `TIMELINE.csv`; do not repeat it here.
+
+## CHARACTER DNA
+Stick figures throughout: plain circle head (no facial features except in a couple of speech-bubble reaction beats), thin single-stroke limbs, no color fill. Identical drawing convention to the host character in every other video already reconstructed in this project. Secondary animals (cat, dog, mouse) use the same simple single-stroke line-art convention, no shading. — OBSERVED
+
+## ENVIRONMENT DNA
+Backgrounds are almost always a flat off-white/light-gray canvas with no horizon or setting except where the gag specifically requires one (the newspaper's cornfield inset, the outdoor tree scenes). No parallax layers, no depth-of-field. — OBSERVED
+
+## OBJECT DNA
+All illustrated objects (globe, sun, seismograph, truck, furniture) are simple black-outline line art on the same flat canvas, redrawn/modified in place rather than replaced with a differently-styled asset when their state changes (e.g. the globe gains cracks and a debris ring but keeps the same base silhouette). — OBSERVED
+
+## COLOR PALETTE
+Overwhelmingly black-line-on-off-white, matching the rest of the project's "xkcd what if" videos. Two deliberate color accents: red, used exclusively for (a) the "xkcd's what if?" bumper/credits card background and (b) hand-scribbled emphasis marks (Richter Scale strikethrough, ruler tick marks, quake epicenter rings). No other color appears. — OBSERVED
+
+## LIGHTING
+Flat, shadowless line-art throughout; no rendered lighting model. — OBSERVED
+
+## CAMERA / FRAMING
+Every shot is a locked, static 2D camera — no pans, zooms, or parallax were measured anywhere in the video. All apparent "movement" is the illustrated subject changing (label swaps, object animation, particle motion), not camera motion. — OBSERVED
+
+## COMPOSITION
+Consistent single-focal-point compositions: one dominant illustration per state, usually paired with a large "MAGNITUDE ##" headline directly above it, and a persistent vertical reference ruler at frame-left for most of the ascending/descending sequence (S05–S12). — OBSERVED
+
+## TYPOGRAPHY
+Two font treatments: (1) a bold, slightly hand-drawn-style sans-serif for the "MAGNITUDE ##" headlines and most captions; (2) a looser, more hand-lettered style for onomatopoeia/sound-effect text (WHUMP, CRASH, PLINK, CLICK, KERTHUMP). Intro question text and LIVE-TV captions sit in light-gray rounded rectangles / black-bordered boxes respectively. — OBSERVED
+
+## GRAPHICS
+Recurring motifs: the vertical "Moment Magnitude" ruler (present from S05 through S12, growing then implicitly continuing off-frame during the descending scale), red hand-scribble emphasis marks, cloud-shaped thought bubbles, small radiating shake-line clusters for impacts, and a reusable explosion-burst graphic (appears 3 times: NYC example, Earth breakup, sun/Magnitude 25). — OBSERVED
+
+## ILLUSTRATION / 3D STYLE
+Pure 2D hand-drawn vector/line-art style; no 3D rendering anywhere, including the "3500 km" tectonic block diagram, which is drawn in a flat isometric-style illustration rather than true 3D. — OBSERVED
+
+## DEPTH
+No true depth layering; foreground/background separation is implied only by relative scale and left/right placement, not by parallax or blur. — OBSERVED
+
+## MOTION LANGUAGE
+Two motion categories only were measured: (1) instantaneous full-composition swaps between magnitude values (the dominant pattern — see `MOTION_EVENTS.csv` RELATIONSHIP=STATE_REPLACEMENT rows), and (2) genuine continuous motion reserved for specific illustrated physics — falling objects (leaf, feather, cat), particle flow (hourglass sand, debris cascade), and explosive/fracturing expansion (Earth breakup, sun burst, magnetar field-line pulse). No decorative camera motion, parallax, glow, or idle-loop animation was found anywhere; none should be added in reconstruction. — OBSERVED
+
+## TRANSITION LANGUAGE
+All 16 shots are joined by hard cuts (`ffmpeg scdet` score ≥5.4 at every shot boundary) except the final shot change into the ending vignette, which uses a brief (~1s) full black-screen wipe (S14→S15 via S15/F15.0). No cross-fades or dissolves were measured. — OBSERVED
+
+## ASSET REUSE PATTERN
+Heavy reuse of a small set of recurring assets across otherwise distinct states: the host stick figure (C01), the vertical ruler (O05), the globe (E03, reused with escalating damage states), the sun (O07, reused with escalating states), the explosion-burst graphic (G03), and the debris/fragment graphic (G04). The "MAGNITUDE ##" text system (T01) is the single most-repeated element in the entire video, appearing in nearly every state. See `ASSET_MANIFEST.csv` OTHER_APPEARANCES column for the full reuse map. — OBSERVED

+[00.000–02.240]
+
+"This is a question from Alex who asks,"
+
+[02.700–06.860]
+
+"what if a Richter magnitude 15 earthquake were to hit America at, let's say, New York City?"
+
+[07.260–09.000]
+
+"What about a Richter 0? Or 25?"
+
+[09.700–13.660]
+
+"Well, given that a magnitude 25 quake would destroy the Sun if one happened there,"
+
+[13.780–15.200]
+
+"it would certainly destroy New York City."
+
+[15.560–16.620]
+
+"But we're getting ahead of ourselves."
+
+[18.660–22.380]
+
+"The Richter scale, which has technically been replaced by the moment-magnitude scale,"
+
+[22.500–23.600]
+
+"measures the strength of an earthquake."
+
+[24.080–25.280]
+
+"Since we usually hear about earthquakes,"
+
+[25.400–27.320]
+
+"which was raiding somewhere between 3 and 9,"
+
+[27.320–30.740]
+
+"a lot of people probably think of 10 as the top of the scale and 0 as the bottom."
+
+[31.180–33.460]
+
+"In fact, there is no top or bottom to the scale."
+
+[33.940–36.480]
+
+"But even if 10 isn't the top of the scale, it might as well be."
+
+[36.880–40.140]
+
+"A magnitude 9 earthquake already measurably alters the rotation of the Earth."
+
+[40.460–43.900]
+
+"The two magnitude 9 plus earthquakes this century both altered the length of the day"
+
+[43.900–45.880]
+
+"by a tiny but measurable fraction of a second."
+
+[46.260–50.700]
+
+"In order to get to magnitude 10, you'd need a ruptured fault line 3 1 1 2,000 kilometers long,"
+
+[51.160–54.380]
+
+"and a magnitude 11 quake would require a fault that went halfway around the world."
+
+[54.380–58.260]
+
+"A magnitude 15 earthquake would be a million times more powerful than that,"
+
+[58.420–61.420]
+
+"and involve the release of enough energy to evaporate all the water on Earth."
+
+[61.720–64.940]
+
+"Though if that happened, we could rest easy knowing the earthquake couldn't cause any tsunamis."
+
+[65.480–70.640]
+
+"Going a few steps further, a magnitude 18 earthquake would release nearly 10 to the 32 jewels of energy,"
+
+[70.800–73.240]
+
+"which is roughly the gravitational binding energy of the Earth."
+
+[73.540–77.300]
+
+"To put it another way, the Death Star caused a magnitude 18 earthquake on Alderon."
+
+[77.700–80.380]
+
+"You could in theory talk about a more powerful earthquake on Earth,"
+
+[80.580–83.320]
+
+"but in practice, all it would mean is that the expanding cloud of space debris"
+
+[83.320–84.500]
+
+"would be faster and hotter."
+
+[85.120–89.140]
+
+"The Sun with its higher gravitational binding energy could have up to a magnitude 24 quake."
+
+[89.340–92.780]
+
+"This is about the energy release you would get if you packed the entire volume of Jupiter"
+
+[92.780–94.920]
+
+"with hydrogen bombs and detonated them all at once."
+
+[95.460–98.840]
+
+"The most powerful quakes in the known universe, which occur in super heavy neutron stars,"
+
+[99.040–99.880]
+
+"are about this magnitude."
+
+[100.380–102.820]
+
+"A magnitude 25 quake would explode the Sun."
+
+[103.380–106.800]
+
+"Hold on, we're spending a lot of time thinking about things that are large and violent."
+
+[107.220–108.460]
+
+"What about the bottom end of the scale?"
+
+[108.860–110.620]
+
+"Does there such a thing as a magnitude 0 earthquake?"
+
+[111.080–113.980]
+
+"Yes, in fact, the scale goes all the way down past zero."
+
+[114.440–118.820]
+
+"Let's take a look at some low magnitude earthquakes with the description of what they would be like if they hit your house."
+
+[119.240–123.320]
+
+"A magnitude 1 quake releases the same energy as dropping a partially loaded cement truck"
+
+[123.320–125.460]
+
+"from 10 meters onto the street in front of your house."
+
+[126.000–129.700]
+
+"A magnitude 0 quake is equivalent to the Dallas Cowboys American football team"
+
+[129.700–132.060]
+
+"running it full-tilled into the side of your neighbor's garage."
+
+[132.660–137.240]
+
+"A magnitude 1 quake is like a single American football player running into a tree in your yard."
+
+[137.240–140.580]
+
+"A cat falling off a dresser would have a magnitude of negative 2."
+
+[141.060–144.320]
+
+"A cat knocking your cell phone off your nightstand would have a magnitude negative 3."
+
+[144.780–147.480]
+
+"Magnitude negative 4 is like a penny falling off of a dog."
+
+[148.100–151.940]
+
+"Magnitude negative 5 is a key press on an IBM Model M mechanical keyboard."
+
+[152.480–154.820]
+
+"Negative 6 is a key press on a lightweight keyboard."
+
+[155.380–158.000]
+
+"Negative 7 is a single feather fluttering to the ground."
+
+[158.520–162.720]
+
+"A fine grain of sand falling onto the pile at the bottom of a tiny hourglass would be a magnitude"
+
+[162.720–164.040]
+
+"negative 8 quake."
+
+[164.380–166.980]
+
+"And let's jump all the way down to magnitude negative 15,"
+
+[167.400–170.060]
+
+"a drifting mode of dust coming to rest gently on a table."
+
+[170.460–173.060]
+
+"Sometimes it's nice not to destroy the world for a change."
+

+# Visual DNA (global rules — see TIMELINE.csv for per-state detail)
+
+## CHARACTER DNA
+- One recurring stick-figure narrator (C01): circle head, no facial features, single-line limbs, holds a paper/clipboard. Appears only in S01 (0–4.42s), static pose throughout.
+- Two decorative sticker vignettes (G04, G05) contain their own tiny line-art figures (mountain/landscape scene; two seated characters), each used exactly once, unrelated in style to C01 (simpler/rounder, no shared model).
+
+## ENVIRONMENT DNA
+- S01: a hand-drawn classroom blackboard on an off-white page background.
+- S02: one continuous oversized hand-drawn world map (E01) — the entire back 79 seconds of the video is a camera move across this single asset, not a sequence of separate map graphics.
+
+## OBJECT DNA
+- Globes (O01/O02) are line-art, gray/white, appear only in S01.
+- City markers (G02) are a single reused dot+label template applied 20 times.
+
+## COLOR PALETTE (E01, the map)
+- Teal — open ocean.
+- Cyan — inland/flooded water or a shallow-sea band.
+- Gray — exposed seabed / bare rock.
+- Yellow (pale) — arid/desert climate band.
+- Green — vegetated/temperate band.
+- Magenta/purple — city marker dots (G02), the only saturated accent color against the muted map palette.
+- Red — the one hand-drawn annotation circle (G03), the only other saturated accent color, used once for emphasis.
+S01 (board scene) is grayscale/off-white only — no color appears until the cut into S02.
+
+## LIGHTING
+Flat, uniform, no shading/gradient beyond the hand-inked line work and flat color fills. No day/night or light-direction cues.
+
+## CAMERA / FRAMING
+- S01: locked-off, no camera movement.
+- S02: a single moving crop window over one large map image. Movement alternates between FAST blurred pan/push bursts (the norm — 8 of 9 transitions) and one slow unblurred pan (A08, ~48–55s). No rotation, no parallax, no depth-of-field change anywhere in the video.
+
+## COMPOSITION
+9:16 vertical throughout. S01 stacks title card (top) / illustration (mid) / character (bottom). S02 has no persistent UI chrome — the map fills the frame edge-to-edge; city labels sit directly on the map near their dot.
+
+## TYPOGRAPHY
+- Title card (T01): black serif, two centered lines, on a rounded gray card — S01 only.
+- Map labels (continent names, city names): hand-lettered look (uneven baseline, marker-style strokes), black, no card/background — S02 only, baked into or overlaid on the map.
+
+## GRAPHICS / ILLUSTRATION STYLE
+Uniform "hand-drawn doodle/whiteboard" style across both shots and both sticker vignettes: black ink outlines, minimal or flat color fill, no gradients, no 3D shading, no photographic elements anywhere in the video.
+
+## MOTION LANGUAGE
+Two motion types only, observed nowhere else:
+1. STATE_REPLACEMENT (object pop-in/swap) — used for O01→O02 and every G02/G03/G04/G05 appearance.
+2. PAN/PUSH with motion blur on the fast bursts, unblurred on the one slow pan (A08) — used only for the S02 camera moves.
+No zoom-breathing, no parallax, no character motion (C01 is static throughout its whole appearance), no particle/glow effects anywhere.
+
+## TRANSITION LANGUAGE
+- S01 internal (F01.0→F01.1): straight content swap on the same locked composition, no visible wipe/fade.
+- S01→S02: the only hard, blurred "whip" transition in the video, corroborated by a ~0.35s audio near-silence dip at the cut point.
+- All S02 internal "cuts" (the scene-detector hits at 8.83/18.0/25.58/35.42/41.92/65.29/72.38s) are NOT shot changes — they are fast-pan motion-blur bursts across the same continuous map asset E01. Treat them as camera moves, not edits.
+
+## ASSET REUSE PATTERN
+E01 (the map) is the backbone: generated/drawn once, reused for the entire second half via camera movement only. G02 (city pin+label) is a single template reused 20 times. Everything else (T01, C01, O01, O02, G03, G04, G05) is single-shot/single-use.
